EXPERIMENT: Hidden-input output clustering after visible-assertion filtering

Purpose. Test unsupervised answer clustering as a verifier reranker. The verifier first executes only the one visible assertion. For visible-passing candidates, it then calls each candidate on the input expression from each remaining MBPP assertion and records the returned values. It never reads or evaluates the expected output expressions. The resulting clusters are used to choose a candidate; existing full-test pass/fail labels are opened only after selection is finalized, to measure the selection strategies offline.

Run and baseline. W&B run `c4fthzd3`, config `configs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-restart-20260929.yaml`, Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct, seed 42, LoRA rank 16, DAPO, learning rate 1e-5, visible_test_count 1, 16 completions per prompt group. Latest saved checkpoint was step 150. Its greedy pass@1 was 0.38449 over all 593 training tasks and 0.38750 over the matched 80 rollout groups.

Data and answer logging. Used the latest 1,280 reward-trace rows as read at the start of the analysis: 80 prompt groups, 16 candidates each, 80 unique task IDs, and two hidden MBPP assertions per task. Candidate calls on hidden test inputs used only the left-hand function-call expression from each assertion; comparator/expected expressions were not read by the verifier or written to the answer log. Visible-passing candidates produced 1,164 logged hidden-input calls; 1,154 returned serializable answers and 10 raised errors or otherwise failed. 68 of 80 groups had at least one visible-passing candidate, and 67 had at least one candidate returning successfully on both hidden inputs. The largest exact two-output cluster averaged 89.3% of fully responding visible-passing candidates in groups where such responses existed. The logged answers are in ignored artifact `outputs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-restart-20260929/consensus-hidden-outputs-step150-window.jsonl`; summary metrics are in `consensus-hidden-output-summary-step150.json`. These logs contain generated outputs and execution status, not expected answers.

Selection rules. For each k, averaged over all uniformly chosen k-subsets of the 16 candidates, preserving candidate order for first-match tie breaks. `visible` selects the first candidate in the subset passing the visible assertion. `static` additionally applies `sandbox.is_hardcoded_lookup` with only the visible assertion. `joint_cluster` selects the earliest candidate in the largest exact cluster of its two hidden-input outputs among visible passers who returned both outputs; if no candidate has both outputs, it falls back to the visible selection. `marginal_majority` computes a unique per-input modal output and selects the candidate matching the greatest number of those modes, with the same visible-selection fallback if there is no usable mode. The full-test oracle selects success whenever a candidate in the subset has a recorded full-test pass.

Results. Rows are k = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The matched checkpoint baseline pass@1 is 38.75%. Full-test oracle pass@k: 35.08%, 44.58%, 53.18%, 60.94%, 67.50%. Visible-first selection scored 35.08%, 42.96%, 48.72%, 52.76%, 56.25%. Visible plus static lookup filter scored the same 35.08%, 42.96%, 48.72%, 52.76%, 56.25%; the static detector again rejected zero visible-passing candidates. Joint two-output clustering scored 35.08%, 43.11%, 49.93%, 55.29%, 60.00%. Per-input modal-output ranking scored 35.08%, 43.11%, 49.88%, 55.17%, 60.00%.

Interpretation and limitations. Both consensus variants beat visible-first selection from k=2 onward, with the largest gain at k=16: 60.00% versus 56.25%, a 3.75 percentage-point improvement. The full-test oracle reached 67.50%, so clustering remained 7.50 points lower. High output agreement did not guarantee correctness: the most common two-output signature was often wrong according to the post-selection full-test measurement. Thus output consensus is a modest reranker, not a correctness verifier. This is one 80-group recent rollout window with candidates from a rolling training period, not 16 generations from one frozen checkpoint. Candidate calls used a 0.7-second timeout at nice 19, serially, and did not pause or modify training. Expected outputs were not used for selection or clustering; recorded full-test status was used only for the final offline score.

Identifiers and environment. Source commit `b4db7dca2bbae4886cae81f9d6d14c1ddaf1e28a`; W&B run `c4fthzd3`; step-150 details and reward trace under `outputs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-restart-20260929/`. GPU: NVIDIA RTX 2000 Ada Generation. No training code or model artifacts were changed.
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Additional post-selection measurement for `EXPERIMENT: Hidden-input output clustering after visible-assertion filtering`. Matched the answer-log groups back to their exact 16-row blocks in the reward trace by task ID sequence. The largest joint output-signature cluster contained at least one full-test-correct candidate in 48/80 groups (60.0%). There was at least one full-test-correct candidate anywhere among the 16 in 54/80 groups (67.5%), so the largest-cluster correct-candidate recall was 48/54 = 88.9% conditional on the 16-sample set containing any correct candidate. The six missed oracle-solvable groups had a correct candidate outside the largest cluster. Full-test labels were consulted only for this post-selection coverage measurement; the clustering itself used only visible-pass status and candidate outputs on the two hidden inputs.

EXPERIMENT: Full-training-set verifier comparison from latest recorded rollout group per task

Purpose. Extend the baseline, full-test oracle, visible-assertion selector, and joint-output-cluster comparison from the 80-task sample to all 593 MBPP training tasks without generating additional model outputs or using the training GPU.

Run and baseline. W&B run `c4fthzd3`; latest saved checkpoint was step 180. Its greedy training pass@1 was 0.39292 over all 593 tasks. Configuration is `configs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-restart-20260929.yaml`, with Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct, seed 42, LoRA rank 16, DAPO, learning rate 1e-5, visible_test_count 1, and 16 generations per prompt.

Candidate selection and data. For each of the 593 tasks, used its most recent complete 16-completion group in the saved reward trace. The trace contained 1,656 prompt groups at analysis time. The latest chosen group was a median 296 prompt groups (about 37 optimizer updates) behind the newest group, the 90th-percentile lag was 802 groups (about 100 updates), and the 99th-percentile lag was 917 groups (about 115 updates). The trace does not record a model checkpoint ID per group, so these candidates do not all come from checkpoint 180. This is a full-task-set analysis of historical rollouts, not a same-checkpoint generation benchmark.

Verifier procedure. For each candidate, executed the visible assertion first. For visible-passing candidates, executed the candidate function on the input expressions from the two remaining MBPP assertions and logged returned outputs without reading their expected expressions. For each k in 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16, averaged over all uniformly selected k-subsets of each task's 16 candidates, preserving candidate order for first-match behavior. `visible` picks the first visible-passing candidate. `joint_cluster` selects the earliest candidate from the largest exact pair-of-outputs cluster among candidates with successful outputs on both hidden inputs, falling back to the visible selection if needed. The full-test oracle reports whether any candidate in the subset passed the full training tests. Full-test statuses were read only after selection to score the verifier. No hidden tests were checked against their expected outputs during verifier selection.

Results. Across all 593 tasks, checkpoint-180 greedy baseline pass@1 was 39.29%. Full-test oracle pass@k for k = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 was 34.13%, 42.69%, 50.33%, 56.93%, and 62.06%. Visible-assertion selection scored 34.13%, 41.51%, 47.29%, 51.39%, and 53.46%. Joint-output clustering scored 34.13%, 41.60%, 48.22%, 53.28%, and 57.00%. At k=16, joint clustering improves 3.54 percentage points over visible-only selection and is 5.06 points below the oracle.

Limitations. The comparison spans all training tasks but uses each task's latest logged rollout group, with substantial and variable lag from the newest model state. The step-180 greedy baseline is therefore not a matched-policy baseline for every candidate group. At k=1, the stochastic rollout candidate pass rate is 34.13%, below the checkpoint greedy score of 39.29%; this is expected to reflect sampling and model-time mismatch, not a calculation error. A same-checkpoint full-set comparison would require generating 9,488 candidates from checkpoint 180 and would compete for GPU resources, so it was not performed.

Artifacts and environment. Hidden-input outputs are in ignored artifact `outputs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-restart-20260929/consensus-hidden-outputs-fulltrain-step180-latestgroup.jsonl`; the summary is `consensus-hidden-output-fulltrain-summary-step180.json`. Source commit `b4db7dca2bbae4886cae81f9d6d14c1ddaf1e28a`; W&B run `c4fthzd3`; GPU: NVIDIA RTX 2000 Ada Generation. Candidate checks ran serially at nice 19, without GPU use or training interruption.

# MBPP checkpoint evaluation comparison

Both selected checkpoints were sampled and evaluated on the same 378 EvalPlus MBPP tasks. The MBPP table scores the original base tests. The MBPP+ table scores the base and extra tests together. Each task has 16 temperature-sampled candidates.

## Checkpoint selection

All 131 saved checkpoint evaluation logs from W&B run `c4fthzd3` were scanned. The MBPP+ winner is step 630. The MBPP base-test winner is step 830. The MBPP values below use the saved greedy checkpoint logs only for checkpoint selection; the tables below are fresh 16-sample evaluations.

| Checkpoint | Selection basis | Saved MBPP pass@1 | Saved MBPP+ pass@1 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 630 | Highest saved MBPP+ greedy eval pass@1 | 64.0% | 54.0% |
| 830 | Highest saved MBPP greedy eval pass@1 | 65.1% | 53.2% |

## Setup and methodology

- Model: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct`, with the LoRA adapter from run `c4fthzd3` at checkpoints 630 and 830.
- Sampling: vLLM 0.10.2, 16 candidates per task, temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, seed 42, maximum 2,048 new tokens, using the repository EvalPlus prompt wrapped in Qwen ChatML.
- Dataset: EvalPlus 0.3.1 MBPP release, 378 tasks, dataset hash `ee43ecabebf20deef4bb776a405ac5b1`.
- Scoring: EvalPlus checked both base and extra tests. `MBPP` success means `base_status == pass`; `MBPP+` success means both base and plus status are pass. Early-exit test checking was enabled, with a 1-second minimum test limit, 4x ground-truth time factor, four workers, and a 2 GiB per-test-process memory limit.
- Execution verifier: test each candidate against the first visible assertion, then select the first visible-passing candidate in each subset, falling back to the earliest candidate if none passes.
- Joint output clustering: among visible-passing candidates, run the candidate on the remaining MBPP base-test inputs without reading expected outputs. Select the earliest candidate in a largest exact typed-output cluster; if no candidate yields a complete signature, fall back to execution selection.
- Selection separation: candidate verifier selections were fixed before full-test labels were read. MBPP labels were used only for the MBPP table; combined base-plus-extra labels were used only for the MBPP+ table.
- Selection caveat: each checkpoint was chosen using greedy pass@1 on the same benchmark family later used for reporting, so these checkpoint-comparison results have selection bias and are not an independent held-out estimate.
- Environment: Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128, NVIDIA RTX 2000 Ada Generation with 16,380 MiB memory. Repository source commit `ba8b794085828aef55d617ac1d2b7a20dd2dee89`.
- Raw candidates, EvalPlus results, verifier selection counts and metrics, and the exact sampling and verifier scripts are in ignored artifact `outputs/mbpp-eval-best-checkpoints-20261003/`.

EXPERIMENT: Checkpoint 830 training-set generation replay and failure analysis

Purpose. Preserve the selected checkpoint's saved greedy training completions outside the transient run logs, execute each saved program on all its training assertions, capture assertion and exception details, and count recurrent failure shapes.

Run and data. W&B run `c4fthzd3`, name `grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-restart-20260929`. Model `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct`, LoRA checkpoint 830, seed 42, rank 16, DAPO, learning rate 1e-5, one visible test in the prompt, 16 rollout generations per prompt group, hybrid reward coefficient 0.75. The original MBPP cache contains 374 train, 90 validation, and 500 test records. After the configured canonical EvalPlus task exclusion, the training pool has 593 tasks. Each checkpoint details row contains one greedy completion and three scorer assertions.

Artifacts and selection. `analysis/checkpoint_830/checkpoint_830_training_generations.jsonl` is a durable copy of all 593 saved checkpoint-830 greedy completions, their saved outcome/reward fields, and full scorer test code mapped from the reward trace. SHA-256: `1a6ea0564ada64eb51035112f3e43618d8edd7dfd577466fd77542bac2b35cce`. No new completions were generated. `analysis/checkpoint_830/checkpoint_830_error_analysis.json` contains each task, all 1,779 assertion outcomes, complete stderr and stdout for failures, actual and expected values when available, reference solution, task text, and pattern membership. SHA-256: `002fb4ab9620456292ad5475546fa8190d6fc27a7ee305914550fefe6d9c3f57`. Selection was not performed; these are the saved greedy completions. Correctness labels were used only for post-training analysis.

Procedure. Loaded task text and reference solutions from the local cached Hugging Face dataset in offline mode. Used `sandbox.split_test_cases` and `sandbox.execute_code` to run each assertion in a fresh isolated-mode Python subprocess and temporary directory, with a three-second timeout. Used eight worker threads. Failed direct comparisons received a second diagnostic execution that evaluated the actual and expected expressions once each and printed their representations. The four-task pilot ran 12 test cases in 0.244 seconds. The full replay covered 593 programs and 1,779 test cases plus 450 comparison diagnostics in 4.891 seconds. The replay command was `HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. python /tmp/replay_checkpoint830.py`; driver SHA-256 at execution: `2010a0125e6b355e56911c36cca18f6eaadee78ca696ad984333eebf018f4b11`.

Results. The replay passed 1,281/1,779 test cases. There were 498 nonpassing cases, comprising 450 assertion mismatches, 45 runtime exceptions, and three syntax errors. At the program level, 372/593 passed all tests, 107 were partial (49 passed one test and 58 passed two), 113 passed none, and one was malformed. Every per-task pass count exactly matched `training-step-830-details.json`. The 450 assertion mismatches were numeric 224, string 79, sequence length 53, sequence content or shape 38, Boolean 23, sequence order 18, set 3, mapping 3, missing/None return 3, and other value mismatches 6. Runtime errors were IndexError 23, TypeError 7, NameError 6, ValueError 6, and re.error 3. Percentages and task membership are in the JSON analysis file.

Training/evaluation context. Exact local training greedy pass@1 values were 32.55% at step 0, 62.73% at step 830, and 70.32% at step 1300. The W&B MCP returned a 100-point sampled evaluation history with EvalPlus greedy pass@1 of 43.9% at step 0, a sampled peak of 54.0% at step 630, 53.2% at step 830, and 52.1% at step 1300. Thus training-pool pass@1 continued to rise after the sampled EvalPlus curve stopped improving; this association is not a causal test of dataset diversity.

W&B curve audit. Run history was retrieved from `kunal-personal/grpo-mbpp`, run `c4fthzd3`. A 50-point sample across internal steps 13,074–250,199 showed `reward/mean` from 0.207 to 0.833, `rewards/reward/std` from 0.350 to 0.497, `training/average_reward` from 0.279 to 0.527, `training/rolling_average_reward` from 0.306 to 0.701, `reward/flat_group_fraction` from 0 to 1, and `reward/mean_group_std` from 0 to 0.323. Sampled `reward/format/mean`, `reward/syntax/mean`, and `reward/interface/mean` were all zero; test-progress and pass components carried reward. Retrieval was sampled, not exhaustive. The exact local checkpoint metrics and complete assertion replay are the reported sources for checkpoint-830 results.

Environment and limitations. Python 3.12.3; 128 CPUs visible; eight replay workers; GPU unused. Sandbox source blob at the replay commit was `c26db028beeb3d2f8a89339108f1d076a958ccce`; repository HEAD was `755dc67e2214aa87f2e1c7efad880abf5affb8a4`. The local subprocess sandbox is not hostile-code isolation. A static AST scan found no obvious filesystem, network, shell, subprocess, or dynamic-evaluation calls in the archived completions. Three assertions per task are not exhaustive behavioral tests. W&B histories were sampled; exact target-step history retrieval was not available through MCP.

EXPERIMENT: Synthetic-task difficulty, repetition, and EvalPlus transfer audit

Purpose. Analyze the saved 10x Luna task artifact, checkpoint greedy evaluations, and GRPO rollout trace to distinguish easier synthetic tasks, task-distribution mismatch, and task-specific overfitting as explanations for the EvalPlus plateau. This is a post-hoc analysis of existing artifacts. No model generation, training, or benchmark scoring was run.

Run and sources. W&B run `mbpp10xluna1007`, run name `grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-10x-luna-20261007`. The mixed training pool has 591 original tasks and 5,319 Luna synthetic tasks. Sources are `analysis/mbpp_category_synthetic_tasks_api10x.jsonl`, `analysis/mbpp_task_taxonomy_10x.json`, `outputs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-10x-luna-20261007/training-step-{0,100,300,400,500,600,660}-details.json`, the corresponding training metrics, `reward-trace.jsonl`, and EvalPlus step results through 660. The reward trace contains 85,632 completion rows across 669 optimizer updates.

Split checkpoint results. The same step-zero model passed all three training assertions on 32.3% of original tasks and 47.0% of synthetic tasks. Mean task reward was 0.410 on originals and 0.675 on synthetics. At step 660, original pass@1 was 43.8% with mean reward 0.517; synthetic pass@1 was 80.7% with mean reward 0.892. Thus both groups improved, while synthetic performance improved much more. The combined training mean reward was 0.854 at step 660, and 90% of rows in that aggregate are synthetic. Each group has three assertions per task, so the gap is not explained by a higher test count for synthetic rows.

Rollout trend. Across the first 100 optimizer steps, sampled mean reward was 0.327 on original completions and 0.440 on synthetic completions. Across steps 501-669 it was 0.400 on original completions and 0.761 on synthetic completions. These are sampled rollout statistics over different task groups, not paired task-level measurements. The per-checkpoint greedy measurements above provide the stronger comparison.

EvalPlus trend. Greedy pass@1 changed from 53.2% MBPP and 44.7% MBPP+ at step zero to 61.1% and 49.7% at step 660. From step 400 to 660, MBPP+ was 49.7% at both endpoints. MBPP changed from 59.5% to 61.1%, with an intermediate high of 61.9%. This supports a late plateau, but the 378-task benchmark is small and the trend alone does not identify a cause.

Task difficulty and distribution signals. Median task-description length was 78 characters for the 591 original tasks and 264 for the synthetics. A simple keyword scan found explicit constraint or edge-case wording in 6.4% of original descriptions and 92.4% of synthetic descriptions; this heuristic is only a wording measure. Median reference-solution AST size was similar, 43 nodes for original tasks and 50 for synthetics, so the higher synthetic pass rate does not establish lower algorithmic complexity. The synthetic pool has 1,207 distinct entry-point names, but it concentrates on recurring task patterns: `count_positive_divisors` occurs 156 times, `count_staircase_ways` 131 times, `collapse_whitespace` 93 times, `is_valid_time` 91 times, and `make_slug` 79 times. The top 20 entry-point names cover 24.7% of synthetic rows. Case-folding descriptions and replacing punctuation with spaces found six internally repeated description classes (12 rows), including repeated divisor-count and every-kth-element specifications. No normalized exact description overlapped the original task descriptions.

Generation repetition and lookup checks. After whitespace normalization, 592 synthetic greedy completions at step zero and 288 at step 660 duplicated a completion assigned to another synthetic task ID; the largest repeated completion group fell from 26 tasks to 17. At step 660, only two original-task completions were duplicated across task IDs. This is consistent with repeated canonical task families, but identical code can also be correct for distinct tasks. The repository's conservative literal-lookup classifier flagged zero checkpoint completions in both groups at steps zero and 660. This classifier misses many possible forms of overfitting and does not rule out template learning or memorization.

Interpretation. The strongest evidence favors an easier and more repetitive synthetic objective that transfers only partly to EvalPlus. The synthetic descriptions are much more explicit, the base model already scores them better, and their pass rate and reward rise much faster. Broad task categories mirror the original pool, so the evidence does not support a major shift in broad programming domains. The wording style and the concentration on recurring task patterns do differ. The trace does not show a collapse in within-task completion variety, and original-task performance improves rather than degrades. It therefore does not establish harmful instance-level overfitting. Over-specialization to the synthetic task templates remains plausible because no held-out synthetic validation set exists.

Limitations and next test. Synthetic references and their three tests were generated together and passed sandbox execution; this checks internal execution, not independent task validity or test coverage. Entry-point repetition and identical completions are indicators, not a semantic-deduplication audit. A controlled follow-up should hold optimizer updates and original-task exposure fixed, reduce the synthetic sampling share, and evaluate both EvalPlus and a separately generated, task-disjoint synthetic validation set. This would separate data difficulty, mixture weighting, and transfer to the generator's task style.

Environment and identifiers. The run's source commit was unavailable in its `run-results.txt`; the local artifacts identify W&B run `mbpp10xluna1007`. EvalPlus set: canonical 378-task MBPP+ v0.2.0. Training and evaluation code were not modified for this audit.

EXPERIMENT: 100 harder-than-example synthetic MBPP tasks and base-model evaluation

Purpose. Generate 100 category-proportional synthetic tasks that are explicitly required to be harder than their three same-category MBPP examples. Measure base Qwen 0.5B pass rate on the generated tasks using the same repository EvalPlus-style prompt and sandbox scoring path as a control evaluation on the earlier 100-task API set.

Task generation. Prompt input `analysis/mbpp_category_api_prompts_harder100.jsonl` contains 100 prompts allocated by largest remainders from the 591-task taxonomy using seed 20261009. Each prompt asks for greater algorithmic or reasoning demands and rejects longer wording or arbitrary restrictions as sufficient difficulty. Three original same-category examples are included. GPT-6 Luna with reasoning effort `none`, 20 concurrent requests, JSON output, and three retries generated task specifications. The generator rejected duplicate descriptions, validated one plain reference function per task, ran each reference against three literal calls in the subprocess sandbox, and materialized the expected-output assertions. All 100 tasks passed reference validation. API usage, including the two-task sanity sample and retries, was 129 responses, 87,074 input tokens, and 79,809 output tokens. Estimated cost was $0.048278. The generated task specs, prompts, materialized tasks, and usage ledger are saved under `analysis/mbpp_category_*_harder100*`.

Difficulty and duplication audit. Median description length is 586.5 characters versus 263 for the earlier easy API100 control. Median reference AST size is 164.5 nodes versus 53.0. These are rough complexity signals, not independent difficulty ratings. The 100 harder descriptions are unique under lowercase and punctuation normalization, with no exact normalized description overlap with the earlier control. The harder set has 88 distinct entry points; its most common entry point occurs four times. The two datasets use the same 13-category allocation but different seeds and sampled examples.

Evaluation method. Generated one greedy completion per task with base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct`, with no adapter, temperature 0, top-p 1, and maximum 2,048 new tokens. Prompt construction used the repository Qwen EvalPlus ChatML wrapper, the task text, and the exact reference function signature; generated assertions were not shown. `sandbox.score_completion` scored each completion against all three materialized assertions with a 3-second timeout. The assertion denominator includes all 300 supplied assertions, including tests that were not executable after syntax-error completions. No candidate selection occurred. The matched easy control is `analysis/mbpp_category_synthetic_tasks_api100.jsonl`, evaluated with the same script and settings. This is an EvalPlus-style prompt and sandbox test of generated tasks, not the official 378-task EvalPlus benchmark.

Results. The harder set had 6/100 fully passing tasks, for greedy task pass@1 of 6.0%. The model passed 67/300 assertions, for an assertion pass fraction of 22.3%. Statuses were 6 passed, 44 partial, 47 failed, and 3 syntax errors. The matched easy API100 control had 45/100 fully passing tasks (45.0%) and passed 196/300 assertions (65.3%). The harder set was 39.0 percentage points lower in full-task pass rate and 43.0 points lower in assertion pass fraction. Category-level counts are in the per-task evaluation JSON.

Interpretation. The prompt change produced a substantially harder set for this base model under the measured greedy protocol. The 44 partial tasks show that many completions still received nonzero assertion-level feedback, but this one-completion-per-task evaluation does not show whether 16-sample GRPO groups will have useful within-group reward variation. Longer specifications and larger references may contribute to difficulty alongside algorithmic demands. Low pass rate alone does not establish that the tasks are unambiguous or independently valid.

Limitations and identifiers. Each generated oracle and its three tests came from the same task-generation response. Sandbox validation proves that the reference runs on those calls, not that task semantics or test coverage are independently correct. This is one 100-task draw, one seed, and one greedy completion per task. Model revision was not pinned. Prompt-generator change commit `6c1ee31`; prompt artifact commit `774994a`; task-generation artifact commit `febde5c`; evaluator assertion-denominator correction commit `5431272`. Evaluation used Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128, vLLM 0.10.2, and one NVIDIA RTX A5000 with 24,564 MiB. Evaluation results are `analysis/mbpp_category_synthetic_harder100_qwen05_eval.json` and matched-control results are `analysis/mbpp_category_synthetic_api100_qwen05_eval_matched.json`.

EXPERIMENT: Sixteen-sample evaluation on the first twenty harder synthetic tasks

Purpose. Measure whether repeated base-model samples produce useful GRPO-style reward variation on the first twenty rows of the new harder-than-example synthetic set. Classify each task as none, all, or mixed according to whether zero, all sixteen, or one to fifteen completions pass all three assertions.

Setup. Input is `analysis/mbpp_category_synthetic_tasks_harder100.jsonl`; tasks were selected as the first twenty rows in file order, with no ground-truth-based selection. The model was base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct`, with no adapter. Each task received sixteen samples using temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, seed 42, and 2,048 maximum new tokens. Prompts used the repository Qwen EvalPlus ChatML wrapper and exact reference function signature. Scoring used the isolated `sandbox.score_completion` path with a 3-second timeout and all three saved assertions. A full pass requires all three assertions to pass. The assertion denominator counts all expected assertions, including assertions skipped after a syntax error. The evaluation script and full 320 completions with per-completion scores are saved in `analysis/evaluate_mbpp_harder20_16gen.py` and `analysis/mbpp_category_synthetic_harder20_16gen_eval.json`.

Results. Of 20 task groups, 13 (65%) had no completion pass all assertions, zero (0%) had all sixteen completions pass, and 7 (35%) had mixed outcomes. There were 11 full-pass completions among 320 (3.44%). Across 960 expected assertions, 157 passed (16.35%). Mean task-level assertion fraction was also 16.35%. The groups with at least one passing completion show that some tasks are solvable by this base model under sampling. The 13 all-zero groups indicate that most of these tasks provided no full-pass success in a group of sixteen, although some still provided partial assertion reward.

Task mix and limits. The first twenty rows cover six arithmetic tasks, thirteen number-theory tasks, and one list task. This is a prefix of a category-proportional dataset, not a representative sample of all thirteen categories. The model is the base model rather than the trained checkpoint. The evaluation uses generated tests and is EvalPlus-style, not the official EvalPlus benchmark. The task, reference, and tests were produced together, and sandbox-valid references do not establish independent semantic validity or test coverage. A single sampling seed and twenty tasks do not support a precise estimate of all synthetic-task group reward distributions.

Environment. Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128, vLLM 0.10.2, NVIDIA RTX A5000 with 24,112 MiB reported memory. Evaluation code and result were produced from source commit `27a7ea389f6189364f4b9b479e01f641db04e25d`; the recorded experiment artifacts are committed separately.

Reward variation detail. Sixteen of the twenty groups had more than one distinct assertion-pass count among their sixteen completions, and sixteen groups had at least one completion pass at least one assertion. Thus, the 13 groups with no complete solution are not all flat zero-reward groups under assertion-fraction scoring. Four groups had no assertion pass in any completion. This is a test-progress signal only; the experiment did not calculate the configured GRPO hybrid reward or inspect optimizer advantages.

EXPERIMENT: One-visible-assertion 16-generation comparison on 100 original and 100 harder synthetic tasks

Purpose. Measure how often a group of sixteen completions produces zero, partial, or full assertion reward on original MBPP tasks and on the harder synthetic tasks. One assertion was visible in each prompt, and all three assertions were scored.

Original set. Used the first 100 original MBPP training-pool rows after canonical EvalPlus exclusion, in repository dataset order. For each task, selected its earliest complete sixteen-candidate group from the saved `c4fthzd3` training trace by task ID and trace order, without inspecting correctness. These original candidates are from the evolving training run, with first occurrences at trace rows 64 to 8,867. The compact saved summary is `analysis/mbpp_original100_saved16gen_eval.json`.

Synthetic set. Used the first 100 rows of `analysis/mbpp_category_synthetic_tasks_harder100.jsonl`. Generated 16 completions per task from the base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct` model without an adapter, at temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, seed 42, and a 2,048-token limit. Prompt construction used `data.build_qwen_evalplus_prompt` with the first assertion visible. Scored all three assertions through the local sandbox and recorded the run's configured hybrid reward: 0.75 times full-pass plus 0.25 times passed-test fraction. The generated completions and per-candidate scores are saved in `analysis/mbpp_category_synthetic_harder100_16gen_visible1_eval.json`. The evaluator is `analysis/evaluate_mbpp_harder20_16gen.py`, which accepts `--task-count 100` and `--visible-test-count 1`.

Task-level score coverage. Rows below count tasks with at least one completion reaching each exact score; rows overlap. Original versus synthetic counts were exactly zero tests, 96/100 (96%) versus 100/100 (100%); exactly one, 36/100 (36%) versus 77/100 (77%); exactly two, 21/100 (21%) versus 32/100 (32%); and exactly three, 68/100 (68%) versus 17/100 (17%). By cumulative threshold, original versus synthetic coverage was at least zero tests, 100/100 versus 100/100; at least one, 84/100 (84%) versus 83/100 (83%); at least two, 80/100 (80%) versus 40/100 (40%); and all three, 68/100 (68%) versus 17/100 (17%).

Group outcomes and signal. By full-task success, original groups were none 32/100 (32%), all sixteen 3/100 (3%), and mixed 65/100 (65%). Synthetic groups were none 83/100 (83%), all sixteen 0/100, and mixed 17/100 (17%). Across all 1,600 completions per set, original passed-test counts were zero 885, one 140, two 84, and three 491; synthetic counts were zero 981, one 490, two 86, and three 43. Under the configured hybrid reward, the synthetic reward varied in 83/100 groups (83%) and was flat zero in 17/100. Original reward varied in 81/100 groups (81%); 16 groups were flat zero and 3 were flat at reward one because all sixteen generations passed. Mean group reward standard deviation was 0.0805 synthetic and 0.2500 original. A one-test-only completion receives reward 1/12 (about 0.083); two tests receive 1/6 (about 0.167); a full pass receives 1.0.

Interpretation. The synthetic tasks are much less likely to produce a full solution under these samples, but their reward is not sparse in the binary sense: 83% of groups have within-group reward variation and partial passing is common. This suggests useful GRPO reward signal for most groups, while 17% of synthetic groups are flat zero and contribute no task-reward preference signal. The signal is weaker in scale and depth than on the original groups, as shown by the lower mean reward standard deviation and much lower two-test and full-pass coverage. This does not prove training will improve held-out evaluation.

Limitations. The original groups come from different points in an evolving training run, while the synthetic groups were generated from a fixed base model. The task sets are not paired, and the first 100 rows have their own category mix. Both use one visible assertion and score three assertions, but this remains a diagnostic of the sampled group reward, not official EvalPlus evaluation. Synthetic references and tests were generated together and are not independently validated. Environment for synthetic generation and scoring: Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128, vLLM 0.10.2, NVIDIA RTX A5000 with 24,112 MiB reported memory. Synthetic evaluator source commit before final metadata correction: `f3a49b0`; original run source commit: `b4db7dca2bbae4886cae81f9d6d14c1ddaf1e28a`.

============================================================================
ANALYSIS: Why the first 100 harder synthetic tasks are harder than the first 100 original MBPP tasks

Purpose and selection. Inspect the actual original and harder synthetic task definitions, not only their pass rates. The original set is the first 100 records in the filtered MBPP training pool, identified by `analysis/mbpp_original100_saved16gen_eval.json`. The synthetic set is the first 100 rows in `analysis/mbpp_category_synthetic_tasks_harder100.jsonl`. The harder prompt inputs and their three example task IDs are in `analysis/mbpp_category_api_prompts_harder100.jsonl`. Original descriptions, references, and tests were read from the local Hugging Face MBPP Arrow cache by task ID. No candidates or task rows were selected using correctness labels.

Descriptive code and specification measures. Original versus synthetic prompt word count mean (median) was 15.1 (14) versus 103.2 (95.5), about 6.8 times as many words. Reference solutions had mean (median) 6.9 (5.5) versus 20.6 (19) nonblank lines, and 52.9 (37.5) versus 186.7 (164.5) Python AST nodes. A loop appeared in 39 versus 91 tasks; a branch appeared in 48 versus 97; nested loop/control-flow depth of at least two appeared in 8 versus 43. Mean loop nodes were 0.6 versus 2.0, and mean branch nodes were 0.8 versus 4.1. The number of functions per reference was similar at about 1.1 in both sets, so the extra structure is mainly inside the task logic. These are descriptive complexity proxies, not direct measures of human difficulty.

Comparison with prompt examples. For 93/100 generated tasks, reference AST size exceeded the median AST size of its three source examples; for 81/100, it exceeded all three. Generated references had more loop nodes than the median source example in 75/100 tasks and more branch nodes in 83/100. These results support the prompt instruction producing more involved code than the examples, but longer reference code can reflect verbosity and generated-oracle choices as well as problem difficulty.

What adds difficulty. Many tasks require several dependent operations and precise ordering. For example, `01-001` computes tiered energy charges, handles consumption above the last numeric band, adds a fixed fee, applies tax, and rounds the result. `06-010` parses quoted comma-separated fields, handles quotes inside quoted fields, and rejects invalid text after a closing quote. `09-006` counts subsets by sum and size while treating equal values at distinct positions separately and reducing modulo a constant. Geometry tasks require polygon clipping or rectangle optimization for concave shapes, and the graph task `12-001` asks for a shortest Hamiltonian path. Many specs add tie rules, boundary conditions, invalid-input behavior, or return conventions that the short original descriptions do not state.

Counterevidence and quality risks. The synthetic descriptions are much more verbose, and some of that length restates assumptions rather than adding useful challenge. Semantic patterns repeat despite unique surface descriptions: `02-002` and `02-004` are near-duplicate divisor-count searches; `11-001` and `11-004` both involve polygon clipping; `11-003` and `11-005` both involve rectangle-union area; and several ranking tasks repeat top-k or nearest-median patterns. Eight entry-point names recur, with a maximum frequency of four. Some tasks lack feasibility bounds: `12-001` is NP-hard for unbounded n, while advanced polygon optimization and divisor-count searches also omit practical size limits. At least one spec, `03-010`, has conflicting reversal rules for a short final block. Excessive complexity, repeated templates, and ambiguous or infeasible requirements can make training harder without improving useful transfer.

Category and sampling caveats. The two task sets span the same thirteen broad categories with broadly similar counts, but are unpaired: for example, the original first 100 contain six arithmetic and six search/sort tasks, while the synthetic first 100 contain six arithmetic and twelve search/sort tasks. Category-matched median reference AST size is higher for synthetic tasks in each category in this sample, but some strata contain very few rows. The first 100 original rows are determined by source dataset order; they are not a random sample. All complexity measures use generated references and do not establish semantic correctness or independent test coverage. The synthetic prompt, generated reference, and three tests were created together. These findings explain why the sampled synthetic set is harder for the base model, but they do not prove that this difficulty will improve EvalPlus transfer.

EXPERIMENT: Category-proportional 10x harder MBPP synthetic-data generation

Purpose. Generate 5,319 harder synthetic tasks to combine with the 591-task original MBPP training pool for 5,910 total rows. Preserve the original category distribution and keep the earlier easier dataset intact.

Setup and generation. Used `analysis/generate_mbpp_category_prompts.py --total-prompts 5319 --harder-than-examples --seed 20261009` and GPT-6 Luna through `analysis/generate_mbpp_category_tasks_api.py`, with reasoning effort `none`, 20 concurrent requests, three literal calls per task, and exact normalized-description deduplication. The first API pass and one retry pass left a small number of malformed JSON responses. A second retry with eleven attempts per failed prompt reused saved validated state. All 5,319 tasks passed reference execution and have three generated assertions. The complete usage ledger includes all retries and replacements.

Category allocation. Arithmetic 342; number theory 702; lists 558; search/sort 612; counting 450; strings 693; sets 180; mappings 450; recurrence/DP 468; matrices 54; geometry 342; graphs 54; predicates 414. Each count is exactly nine times the matching original category count.

Cost and time. The generator made 6,574 API responses, using 4,142,031 input tokens, 73,967 cached input tokens, and 3,602,069 output tokens. At the recorded GPT-6 Luna rates, estimated cost was $2.208581. Active generator command time across the three attempts totaled 2,920.662 seconds, or 48 minutes 40.7 seconds; end-to-end wall time was about 54 minutes. Detailed accounting and hashes are in `analysis/mbpp_harder5319_generation_summary.json`.

Preflight and training instrumentation. The matched config loaded 5,910 training rows and 378 EvalPlus rows with one visible assertion, using a fresh HF dataset cache after the default cache exposed a zero-byte parquet. Added W&B per-step curves for the mean fraction of task generations passing at least one, two, and three tests. Per-task counts and fractions are written to the training output's `task-coverage-trace.jsonl` with task ID and optimizer step. Targeted training and sandbox tests passed: 28 passed. The user directed that the separate 16-generation base-model evaluation be skipped.

Selection and limitations. All generated tasks were kept after exact normalized-description deduplication; no ground-truth outputs were used to select tasks. Each generated reference and its three assertions were produced together, so the assertions are not an independent oracle. Exact text uniqueness does not rule out semantic repetition. No training checkpoint has been selected using EvalPlus results; checkpoint selection is disabled.

One-time prelaunch cleanup. Before training, removed 65 older checkpoints, steps 10 through 650, from the inactive easier-data run. Verified and retained its latest complete checkpoint at step 660. This reclaimed 7,940,414,189 logical bytes (7.395 GiB). No checkpoints will be deleted after the harder-data run starts.

Training launch. Started the separate harder-data run from the base model at 2026-10-09 07:46:46 UTC with W&B run ID `mbpphard10x1009` in `kunal-personal/grpo-mbpp`. The configuration preserves the linked run's optimizer, batch sizes, GRPO reward, seed, 50,000-step target, and save/evaluation cadence; it changes the synthetic data path and run identity. The ten-minute supervisor is running as PID 34560. On failure it records a diagnosis and resumes from the latest complete checkpoint in the new output directory. No checkpoint cleanup will occur after launch. W&B URL: https://wandb.ai/kunal-personal/grpo-mbpp/runs/mbpphard10x1009.

EVALPLUS TREND COMPARISON: ORIGINAL MBPP, EASY SYNTHETIC MIX, AND HARDER SYNTHETIC MIX

Purpose and setup. Compare W&B EvalPlus greedy pass@1 across three Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct GRPO runs at matched optimizer steps. The original-only run is `c4fthzd3` with config `configs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-restart-20260929.yaml` and 593 original MBPP tasks. The easy-synthetic mix is `mbpp10xluna1007` with config `configs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-10x-luna-20261007.yaml`, 591 original plus 5,319 tasks from `analysis/mbpp_category_synthetic_tasks_api10x.jsonl`. The harder-synthetic mix is `mbpphard10x1009` with config `configs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-10x-harder-luna-20261009.yaml`, 591 original plus 5,319 tasks from `analysis/mbpp_category_synthetic_tasks_harder5319.jsonl`. All three configs use seed 42, learning rate 1e-5, one visible assertion, and EvalPlus MBPP+ test evaluation. W&B histories were read on 2026-10-10. Each saved evaluation point every ten steps was used for ordinary least squares slope fits; slopes below are percentage points per 100 optimizer steps. The matched table uses evaluations exactly at each 100-step mark.

Matched pass@1 values, formatted as MBPP / MBPP+. Step 0: original-only 0.519 / 0.439; easy mix 0.532 / 0.447; harder mix 0.524 / 0.437. Step 100: 0.550 / 0.466; 0.550 / 0.471; 0.537 / 0.455. Step 200: 0.593 / 0.492; 0.593 / 0.479; 0.553 / 0.468. Step 300: 0.601 / 0.508; 0.590 / 0.479; 0.556 / 0.481. Step 400: 0.598 / 0.508; 0.595 / 0.497; 0.574 / 0.500. Step 500: 0.624 / 0.519; 0.608 / 0.492; 0.582 / 0.503. Step 600: 0.630 / 0.524; 0.611 / 0.503; 0.566 / 0.495. Step 700: 0.638 / 0.529; easy mix has no later history; harder mix 0.598 / 0.511. Step 800: 0.635 / 0.524; easy mix has no later history; harder mix 0.608 / 0.511. Step 900: 0.635 / 0.521; easy mix has no later history; harder mix 0.619 / 0.529. At step 970, harder mix reports 0.603 / 0.519, while the original-only run reports 0.624 / 0.519.

Trend slopes. Over steps 0-970, the original-only run's fitted MBPP and MBPP+ slopes are +1.01 and +0.70 points per 100 steps. The harder mix's slopes are +0.96 and +0.86 points per 100 steps. Over the shared late interval 600-970, original-only slopes are +0.07 and -0.26, while harder-mix slopes are +1.12 and +0.88. Over the original-only run's full observed interval 600-1300, the fitted slopes are -0.03 and -0.14. The easy mix ends at step 660; over its full 0-660 history the slopes are +1.17 and +0.74, and over steps 600-660 they are approximately 0.00 and -0.86. The harder mix is not a straight rising line at every segment: its fitted slopes are +1.48 / +1.63 over 0-300, +0.92 / +0.66 over 300-600, and +1.12 / +0.88 over 600-970.

Interpretation and limits. The harder-mix curve rose again after its step-600 dip and has a clearly positive late slope, while the original-only run was flat or slightly down after step 600. This supports the visual impression of a stronger late upward trend for the harder mix. At step 970, however, MBPP remains 2.1 points below original-only and MBPP+ is tied. Across 0-970, MBPP slopes are nearly the same, while the harder mix has the larger MBPP+ slope. The easy mix has no observations after step 660, so its trend cannot be compared at step 900 or 970. These are observational comparisons, not a controlled causal test: the original-only dataset has 593 tasks while each synthetic mix has 5,910, so the same optimizer step represents different data reuse; initial EvalPlus scores also differ slightly across runs; and run histories may have independent runtime or evaluator variability. Stepwise score changes are noisy because EvalPlus contains 378 tasks. The current W&B run `mbpphard10x1009` was running at step 970 when queried; the step-970 checkpoint is complete. Its training-set metrics are pass@1 0.1854484 and average reward 0.4059222. Its 16-generation coverage averages across eight task groups are 0.7578125 with at least one test passed, 0.2734375 with at least two, and 0.21875 with all three.

## Old-run generation and evaluation failure audit

Experiment identifier. Original-only GRPO run `c4fthzd3`, local output `outputs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-restart-20260929`. The run used Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct with LoRA rank 16, learning rate 1e-5, 16 samples per task, one visible assertion, and three scored assertions per task. Local reward trace contains 168,960 completions across 1,320 steps and 593 task IDs. Code revision before this audit was `970c98ef45468ec99895ae446e35baf6adbc5deb`.

Purpose. Inspect saved late training generations and compare selected successful and failed held-out evaluation cases to identify signs of memorization, shortcut heuristics, or gaps in algorithmic generalization.

Method and selection. Used only saved outputs. Mapped each 128-row reward-trace batch to its training step. Inspected task 343 at steps 1200 and 1320, task 434 at step 1100, and task 650 at step 1300. Compared saved completion code with each task's ordered assertions. For held-out evaluation, inspected the stored step-1300 EvalPlus results and training evaluation details. Selected examples by visible failure pattern and task type. No model generation or sandbox execution was run for this audit. Candidate selection did not use hidden ground-truth solutions. Benchmark pass and failure labels were read from the saved EvalPlus evaluation after selection.

Results. At step 1300, training-set greedy pass@1 was 0.703 across 593 tasks, with 417 full passes and average assertion reward 0.791. EvalPlus MBPP pass@1 was 239/378 or 0.632. MBPP+ pass@1 was 197/378 or 0.521. The raw `plus_status` field marks 199 tasks as passing the added tests, but the complete MBPP+ rate requires passing both base and added tests. Forty-two tasks passed MBPP base tests and failed added MBPP+ tests. The run's saved step-1300 benchmark report is `outputs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-restart-20260929/evalplus/step-1300/mbpp_results.txt`; per-task outputs are in `evalplus/step-1300/mbpp/qwen2_chat_temp_0.0/eval_results.json`.

Late training generations showed repeated plausible but incorrect algorithms. At steps 1200 and 1320, all 16 samples for task 343 `dig_let` received 0/3. Samples counted digits first and letters second, while the saved assertions expected letters first. At step 1300, all 16 task 650 `are_Equal` samples received 2/3. Inspected samples used positional equality. They fail the first visible assertion, which treats reversed arrays as equal, while matching the two hidden assertions that expect unequal arrays to return false. At step 1100, 14/16 samples for `text_match_one` received 2/3. The inspected code recognized a matching substring but returned `Matched!` where the positive test expected `Found a match!`. These samples do not show visible-assertion lookup behavior. They show inconsistent specifications or expected conventions and repeated shallow interpretations.

Successful evaluation samples included MBPP/757 reverse-string pair counting, MBPP/250 tuple occurrence counting, MBPP/238 substring counting, and MBPP/556 counting pairs with odd XOR. These solutions used direct loops and counters and passed both MBPP and MBPP+. Failed samples exposed specific gaps. MBPP/6 checked whether XOR was nonzero rather than whether it had exactly one set bit. MBPP/245 used a local-peak approach that failed the bitonic subsequence examples. MBPP/63 computed a minimum absolute difference rather than the requested maximum difference. MBPP/721 inspected local neighboring cells instead of constructing complete paths. MBPP/9 returned zero for a repeated-character string even though the required rotation count is positive. Among base-pass, plus-fail examples, MBPP/459 removed uppercase characters rather than uppercase substrings, and MBPP/752 hard-coded early Jacobsthal values before using an incorrect recurrence.

Interpretation and limits. The inspected samples contain no clear hard-coded test-input lookup. The strongest pattern is reliable performance on direct counting tasks and failures on multi-step dynamic programming, path reasoning, semantic distinctions, and edge conditions. This is consistent with a generalization or task-understanding gap, but the hand-selected sample cannot estimate prevalence or prove the absence of memorization. Old reward traces record aggregate passed-test counts rather than a per-assertion bitmap, so visible versus hidden attribution is static and certain only for manually inspected cases such as task 650.

## Per-assertion outcome logging change

Purpose. Preserve the result of every scored assertion and label it visible, hidden, or unknown so future training runs can directly measure whether rollouts pass the prompt-visible assertion or only hidden reward assertions.

Implementation. `sandbox.py` now stores ordered `test_results` in each scoring detail. Each row contains a one-based test index, visibility label, pass boolean, execution status, and test case. Formatting and syntax failures retain one `not_run` row per known assertion. The training reward closure passes the configured `visible_test_count`; model evaluation passes the same prompt visibility count. Rollout trace rows therefore preserve per-test outcomes, and W&B step logs expose separate visible and hidden assertion pass fractions and counts. The existing aggregate reward and task coverage fields remain available.

Safety boundary. The active training process was not signaled, stopped, restarted, or modified. The code change is loaded by future Python launches. Existing saved traces are unchanged and still require replay for per-assertion outcomes.

Validation. `pytest -q tests/test_sandbox.py tests/test_evaluate.py` passed 29 tests. `pytest -q tests/test_train.py` passed 9 tests. A full `pytest -q` run produced no test failure but stalled in `pathlib` for 153 seconds and was interrupted. `git diff --check` passed. The targeted test runs were local and did not invoke training.

## Problem-type comparison of step-1300 training and EvalPlus generations

Experiment identifier. Original-only run `c4fthzd3`, local output `outputs/grpo-mbpp-fulltrain-8x16-b128-micro2-workers8-0.5b-50000-dual-greedy-evalplus031-visible1-save10-restart-20260929`.

Purpose. Compare problem types solved and failed by saved training-set greedy completions and saved held-out EvalPlus completions at step 1300, to explain the train/evaluation gap.

Setup and selection. Used `training-step-1300-details.json` for all 593 training tasks and `evalplus/step-1300/mbpp/qwen2_chat_temp_0.0/eval_results.json` for 378 held-out MBPP tasks. Joined task IDs to cached MBPP Arrow task descriptions and EvalPlus prompts. No generation or execution was run. Categories are coarse, mutually exclusive lexical bins assigned from task wording. The same binning was used on both sets. Benchmark labels are the saved outcomes; training pass means all three scored assertions passed. EvalPlus MBPP+ means passing both base and added tests.

Metrics by category. Training pass rate and EvalPlus base and complete Plus pass rates were: numeric/math, 133/186 (71.5%), 103/158 (65.2%), 82/158 (51.9%); list/tuple/set, 73/102 (71.6%), 46/67 (68.7%), 41/67 (61.2%); string, 78/114 (68.4%), 45/64 (70.3%), 36/64 (56.3%); algorithmic/search/order, 65/96 (67.7%), 24/48 (50.0%), 21/48 (43.8%); other, 36/54 (66.7%), 10/21 (47.6%), 8/21 (38.1%); matrix/nested, 21/27 (77.8%), 9/17 (52.9%), 9/17 (52.9%); dictionary/counting, 11/14 (78.6%), 2/3 (66.7%), 2/3 (66.7%). Overall, training passed 417/593 (70.3%), EvalPlus MBPP passed 239/378 (63.2%), and complete MBPP+ passed 197/378 (52.1%). The raw `plus_status` field alone reports 199 pass, including two cases that do not pass the base suite; this is why complete Plus uses the intersection.

Observed patterns. Direct counting, routine container operations, and arithmetic have relatively high training success. Evaluation is weakest on algorithmic/search/order tasks, where half pass base and 43.8% pass the complete Plus suite. Saved failures include merging three sorted lists by concatenating them without sorting the combined list, an incorrect single-branch Eulerian-number recurrence, and an incomplete binary-string rotation search. Training failures show a similar algorithmic weakness, such as solving “no three consecutive elements” by selecting a length-three window instead of optimizing over allowed subsets. Among 42 saved tasks that pass the base suite but fail added Plus tests, several solutions are plausible on standard cases but mishandle edge conditions or semantics. Examples include snake-to-camel conversion that changes interior capitalization, tuple-to-integer conversion that mishandles multi-digit entries, and minimum-of-three comparisons that mishandle ties.

Interpretation and limitations. The artifacts support a capability and coverage gap: routine patterns transfer better, while multi-step algorithms, exact task interpretation, and edge cases fail in both settings and more often in held-out evaluation. This is evidence for limited generalization, not proof of memorization. Training and EvalPlus sets have different task mixes, categories are lexical approximations, and the category samples vary in size. The comparison is observational and cannot isolate dataset distribution from evaluation-suite difficulty.

## Single-task rejection sampling plus SFT pilot implementation

Purpose. Add a bounded pilot for the requested iterative method: sample 16 completions for one MBPP task, keep only completions that pass every original assertion, train for one response-only causal cross-entropy epoch on retained completions, and repeat sampling and SFT for up to five cycles. The pilot stops early when greedy decoding passes all three tests or when a cycle produces no accepted solution.

Implementation. Added `experiments/rejection_sampling_sft.py`. It loads a cached MBPP task, supports a base model or PEFT checkpoint, samples in batches of at most two to bound generation memory, scores through the existing sandbox, saves all candidates with per-test results, saves adapters after each cycle, and logs sample pass rate, accepted counts, SFT loss, greedy pass, and timing metrics to a separate W&B run. Defaults select original task 621, which has three assertions and does not overlap the canonical EvalPlus task IDs. The model and task are configurable. The script limits runs to one task, exactly 16 generations per cycle, and at most five cycles.

Validation. `python -m py_compile experiments/rejection_sampling_sft.py` and `--help` passed. Loading task 621 from the cached MBPP Arrow data returned exactly three assertions, and its ID is outside the EvalPlus set. No generation or SFT was started during implementation. At validation, the active GRPO run was at training step 1134, and a GPU sample showed 83% utilization with 8.7 GiB in use. The live run remains untouched. Before running the GPU pilot, recheck that its memory and compute use fit the requested low-impact constraint.

Pilot correction note. The first three pilot launches exposed a response-boundary bug: generated completions ended with a closing Markdown fence, and the pilot passed the fence without an opening fence to the shared extractor. The sandbox therefore parsed empty code and reported zero passing tests. Those zero-acceptance metrics are invalid and were not used as evidence about the policy or rejection sampling. The initial launches did successfully generate and save 16 raw candidates per selected task. The script now strips generated fence markers and explicitly wraps code for sandbox scoring. The task-924 candidates are being rescored from the saved raw generations, so no new sampling is needed for that batch. The training process was left running.

Corrected candidate rescore. The 16 saved task-621 responses contain 0 full passes, task 889 contains 4/16 full passes, and task 924 contains 16/16 full passes after code-fence normalization. Re-scored greedy completions show task 621 at 0/3, task 889 at 3/3, and task 924 at 3/3. Task 889 was selected by its task wording before looking at candidate outcomes. Its first sample rate is 25%, while greedy already passes, so it can measure improvement in sampled pass rate but cannot show greedy pass@1 rising from zero. Updated the pilot stop condition to continue sampling after a greedy pass until the sampled rate reaches 100% or the five-cycle limit is reached. The prior zero-pass measurements remain invalid due to the fence parsing bug.

W&B pilot run links. All pilot runs are in the existing project `kunal-personal/grpo-mbpp`: cache-load failure `5c3klshl` (failed), invalid-fence runs `7arte3nf`, `4bppvdgr`, and `ct8ugffi` (finished with invalid zero acceptance), and iterative task-889 run `efr6mtam` (failed during SFT optimizer setup because the adapter loaded frozen). The task-889 run had a corrected initial greedy pass and 4/16 corrected accepted examples before failing to create an optimizer. Added `is_trainable=True` when loading the PEFT checkpoint. The live GRPO run is separate and remains active.

Low-impact execution adjustment. During the iterative W&B run `efr6mtam`, the active GRPO process was still evaluating checkpoint step 1130, and GPU use was 22.5 GiB of 24.6 GiB. The iterative pilot failed at SFT setup before any gradient update because the loaded adapter was frozen; it had 4 accepted examples from task 889. The script now enables trainable adapter loading and supports CPU execution with a configurable single-thread default, plus reuse of a saved baseline greedy completion. The next attempt will use one CPU thread at low process priority while the GRPO evaluation owns the GPU. This avoids further GPU contention.

## Single-task rejection sampling reaches a 100% sample pass rate

Purpose. Continue the task-889 rejection sampling and SFT pilot until a fresh sample batch has a 100% full-pass rate. The CPU pilot had reached 9/16 (56.25%) in cycles 2 and 3, so this run started from its saved cycle-3 adapter.

Setup and selection. The task was selected from its prompt wording before candidate outcomes were inspected. The source is cached original MBPP task 889, with its three original assertions. Each candidate was selected for SFT only when all three assertions passed in the repository sandbox. This is task-specific supervised filtering, so the resulting pass rate measures the same task assertions used for rejection. The greedy result was scored separately before and after the update. No EvalPlus or other held-out benchmark score is claimed.

Command. `python experiments/rejection_sampling_sft.py --model outputs/rejection-sampling-sft-task889-cpu-iterative-step1120/adapter-cycle-3 --task-id 889 --resume-greedy outputs/rejection-sampling-sft-task889-cpu-iterative-step1120/greedy-cycle-3.json --output-dir outputs/rejection-sampling-sft-task889-cuda-step1120 --wandb-run-name mbpp-rejection-sampling-sft-task889-cuda-step1120 --device cuda --max-cycles 5 --target-sample-pass-rate 1.0`.

Configuration. The model was `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct` with the task-889 CPU cycle-3 LoRA adapter as input. The script used 16 samples per cycle, batch size 2, temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, a 512-token generation limit, BF16, seed 42, a 3-second sandbox timeout, and response-only AdamW training at learning rate 1e-5 for one epoch on the accepted candidates. The configured maximum was five cycles, with an early stop at a 100% sample pass rate. The run used the visible NVIDIA RTX A5000 with 24,564 MiB, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128, Transformers 4.56.2, PEFT 0.21.2, and Python 3.12. The GPU had no other visible process when the pilot started. A separate GRPO job was reported in another session; its GPU was not visible to this process.

Results. Cycle 1 passed 16/16 candidates (100%), compared with CPU cycle 3 at 9/16 (56.25%), an increase of 43.75 percentage points. All 16 candidates passed all three assertions. The inherited adapter's greedy completion passed 3/3 before sampling, and the updated adapter's greedy completion passed 3/3. The cycle accepted 16 candidates, then completed one SFT epoch with mean loss 0.0797623 in 2.55 seconds. Generation took 29.70 seconds, scoring took 0.93 seconds, and the full cycle took 30.63 seconds. The run stopped after cycle 1 because its target was met.

Artifacts and identifiers. The source adapter is `outputs/rejection-sampling-sft-task889-cpu-iterative-step1120/adapter-cycle-3`. The final adapter is `outputs/rejection-sampling-sft-task889-cuda-step1120/adapter-cycle-1`. ## Eight-task rejection-sampling SFT pilot stopped at 75%

Purpose. Extend the task-889 rejection-sampling experiment to eight MBPP tasks and raise the per-cycle full-pass sample rate to 100%. The run was stopped at the user's request after the corrected experiment reached a stable 75% ceiling and exposed that two tasks produced no full-pass candidates.

Setup and selection. The model was `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct`, initially loaded from the local base snapshot at `outputs/rejection-sampling-sft-task889-base-cuda-20261010/base-model`. The eight task IDs were 370, 888, 461, 670, 953, 525, 685, and 834. They were selected with a seeded prompt-only draw after excluding task 889 and the EvalPlus task IDs. Each task has 16 candidates per cycle. The sandbox scores each candidate against all three original assertions for that MBPP task, and SFT accepts only candidates that pass all three. `rs/sample_pass_rate` is the number of full-pass candidates divided by 128 for that cycle. Greedy pass rate is logged separately. Tests were not changed. Task 461's prompt asks for the number of uppercase characters, but original assertions expect 1 for both `PYthon` and `BigData`, each of which contains two uppercase characters. Task 370 is consistent, but its candidates mostly sort the numeric strings lexically and in ascending order instead of numerically in descending order.

Configuration and environment. The batch used BF16, seed 42, temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, maximum generation length 512 tokens, generation batch size 16, three-second sandbox timeout, AdamW learning rate 1e-5, one response-only SFT epoch per cycle, target rate 1.0, and a 20-cycle limit per process. The first process used the default right-padding behavior and was stopped after cycle 12 when the decoder-only padding warning was identified. The corrected process set tokenizer padding to left and resumed from the saved cycle-11 adapter. It ran on an NVIDIA RTX A5000. Runtime versions were Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128, CUDA 12.8, Transformers 4.56.2, and PEFT 0.21.2. Code commit `4156414` (`Make rejection sampling checkpoints opt-in`) contains both the default-off checkpoint flag and the left-padding correction. The corrected command added `--save-checkpoints` explicitly.

Results. The right-padded base run had initial greedy pass 0/8. Its per-cycle candidate pass counts were 23, 20, 26, 27, 36, 45, 46, 47, 50, 52, 51, and 62 out of 128 for cycles 1 through 12. Cycle 12 was 62/128 (48.44%). W&B run `wwof07iy` records this process. The corrected restart had initial greedy pass 4/8. Its per-cycle counts for cycles 1 through 20 were 59, 62, 74, 84, 87, 96, 96, 96, 96, 96, 96, 96, 96, 96, 95, 96, 95, 96, 96, and 96 out of 128. Its best and final sample rate was 96/128 (75%). In cycle 20, tasks 525, 670, 685, 834, 888, and 953 passed 16/16 candidates each; tasks 370 and 461 passed 0/16 each. W&B run `zo548clg` records the corrected restart. The user explicitly stopped the process during the cycle-20 SFT update, before cycle-20 greedy evaluation or adapter save. Cycle 19 is the latest complete saved adapter.

Artifacts and separation. The right-padded run's candidate and greedy logs are under `outputs/rejection-sampling-sft-mbpp-8task-base-20261011/run`; completed adapters 8 through 11 remain there. Task 461's original tests conflict with the task description. The user requested keeping all original tests unchanged and stopping the run, so no replacement task or test correction was made. The first process's candidate results are affected by right padding and should not be treated as an equivalent corrected run. The corrected run's cycle-20 SFT update was interrupted and is not represented by a completed checkpoint.

Metric definition correction recorded 2026-10-11: the user clarified that a passing completion in the generated-solution cache substitutes for a model response in each requested candidate slot. The preceding `zriwfwol` pilot reported only actual model generations as the sample-rate denominator. Its 2/40 and 1/30 figures are model-generation-only diagnostics, not the requested cache-inclusive sample pass rate. The updated pilot records both quantities. `rs/sample_pass_rate` counts actual passing generated candidates plus one cached passing response for each requested sample slot on a cached task. `rs/candidate_equivalents` records that denominator. `rs/model_generated_sample_pass_rate` and `rs/generated_candidates` isolate fresh model output. Purpose: Train a fresh LoRA adapter on one accepted passing solution per original MBPP training task, using existing cache entries and one initial candidate-collection phase, then keep training until manually stopped or the configured one-million-epoch ceiling is reached.

Metric audit, first rejection-SFT epoch, 2026-10-11 UTC: Training W&B run `9a4kifss` is https://wandb.ai/kunal-personal/grpo-mbpp/runs/9a4kifss. At epoch 1 / step 47, official EvalPlus reported MBPP pass@1 0.058 and MBPP+ pass@1 0.040. The simultaneously displayed `mbpp_tests_pass_fraction` 0.9114 and `mbpp_plus_tests_pass_fraction` 0.9137 were incorrect. `train.canonical_test_pass_metrics` subtracted the length of `base_fail_tests` / `plus_fail_tests` from the test count even when EvalPlus did not execute tests and marked the task failed with an empty failure list. There were 317 non-passing task records with an empty failure list; the code therefore counted every assertion in those records as passed. Recalculation from the same EvalPlus result file, treating a failed task with no executed-test details as zero passed tests, gives MBPP test pass fraction 89/1,174 = 0.07581 and MBPP+ 3,139/41,015 = 0.07653. The official task pass@1 remains 5.8% / 4.0%. Many failing EvalPlus records contain an empty generated `Code:` body, consistent with tests not running. This discrepancy is a metric implementation bug, not a real 90% test success rate.

Metric fix: `train.canonical_test_pass_metrics` now requires an EvalPlus `pass` status before treating all tests as passed. A failed task contributes partial successes only when EvalPlus reports actual failing-test details. The corrected epoch-one values were verified from the saved raw EvalPlus artifact. The active Trainer process had already imported the old function when this audit was performed, so this code correction will apply after any future monitor restart; the currently active process must not be stopped under the standing user instruction. Until it restarts, its subsequent `mbpp_tests_pass_fraction` values may retain the same defect. Other full EvalPlus task pass@1 fields are from EvalPlus's official result and are not affected.

Root-cause diagnosis and format-corrected restart, 2026-10-11 UTC: Epochs 1 through 3 of the first rejection-SFT attempt collapsed from official EvalPlus MBPP pass@1 5.8% to 1.3% to 0.5%, while the full-task training pass@1 fell from 4.1% to 1.0% to 0.17%. The checkpointed `data.build_sft_dataset` target was malformed for this dataset. Each normalized Qwen prompt already ends with the assistant prefix ` ```python\n`, but the SFT target prepended `Code: \n```python\n` and appended another fence. The official EvalPlus decoder stops at `\n````. The model therefore learned to emit the `Code:` label followed by a newline and redundant fence, and evaluation cut the completion off before any code. Raw epoch-one EvalPlus samples confirm many outputs were exactly `Code:\n`; this directly explains the 317 failed task results with no executed-test detail and the collapse. The separately fixed test-pass-fraction implementation addresses the misleading 90% assertion values but does not fix the model collapse.

Fix: `build_sft_dataset` now supports configured completion prefix/suffix values while preserving the previous default for other callers. The corrected rejection-SFT config sets both values empty, so the target is only the clean cached solution body and matches the already-open Python fence in the prompt. A focused tokenizer test verifies the continuation has no redundant `Code:` label or code fence. Validation: all 9 tests in `tests/test_data.py` passed; Python and supervisor shell syntax checks passed; a local tokenizer smoke test on a real cached solution confirmed the target begins with raw Python code. The broken trainer is being explicitly stopped and restarted from the original configured base model with the same 371 accepted solutions and no new candidate sampling. The old attempt's checkpoints remain preserved in its original output directory. The restart uses a new W&B run and a separate output/checkpoint directory. No GRPO checkpoint or original MBPP test is changed.

Format-fix restart launch, 2026-10-11 19:53 UTC: Explicitly stopped the malformed-format trainer after epoch 3 (latest preserved checkpoint `checkpoint-141` in the first attempt's directory) and stopped its supervisor. No old checkpoint was deleted. The corrected run started from the original local base model with a fresh LoRA adapter, not from the corrupted-format checkpoint. It uses new isolated output `outputs/rejection-sampling-sft-original-only-formatfix-20261011` and new checkpoint directory `outputs/rejection-sampling-sft-original-only-formatfix-20261011/full-training/checkpoints`. It reuses the completed candidate collection summary and the existing shared solution map, with 371 accepted original-task solutions; it does not regenerate candidates. Corrected training W&B run ID `9jx98cdg` is https://wandb.ai/kunal-personal/grpo-mbpp/runs/9jx98cdg. Supervisor PID 803833 and trainer PID 803842 were active at launch. The first ten-step training loss values were 0.2829, 0.2486, 0.2097, and 0.2104; the epoch-one full evaluation is pending. The ten-minute monitor and checkpoint restart loop are active.

Format-fix validation, epoch 1, 2026-10-11 19:56 UTC: The corrected run completed its full evaluation at step 47. EvalPlus MBPP pass@1 is 0.519 (196/378) and MBPP+ pass@1 is 0.429 (162/378). Full original training-set greedy pass@1 is 0.3350 (198/591). The corrected assertion pass fractions are 0.5647 for MBPP and 0.5774 for MBPP+. All 378 saved epoch-one EvalPlus completions are non-empty and none begins with a redundant `Code:` label or code fence. These results confirm the output-format mismatch was the cause of the empty-completion collapse. The first run had fallen to MBPP 0.005 / MBPP+ 0.003 by epoch 3. The format-fixed run started from base and is continuing under its ten-minute supervisor. W&B: https://wandb.ai/kunal-personal/grpo-mbpp/runs/9jx98cdg. The source/config/test fix is commit `04ccd73`; the live-run record is commit pending.
