## Validation provenance audit during the existing-model comparison

Purpose: Identify whether a later learned combiner could use a genuinely unseen non-test calibration source without retraining the existing members. This was a read-only source and code audit. No dataset rows, official test examples, model scoring, or label generation were performed.

The original unqualified Jina checkpoint has epoch 6 and optimizer step 3378. Its original log identifies W&B run a7bwo46l and 9000 preference training rows. The step count matches six epochs at effective batch size 16. The notes state that SFT label extraction did not alter that active preference run. This supports preference-only warm-start provenance, although a cryptographic training-data manifest was not saved.

A candidate later validation source would combine question-disjoint released SFT cases and non-Live BFCL cases. It is not ready as gold calibration data. Exact question exclusions do not remove all rewritten APIGen ancestry. Combining SFT-only refusal and clarification cases with BFCL-only tool cases also confounds class and source. Non-Live BFCL examples can have been seen during upstream public pretraining even if our task training excluded them.

The When2Call paper describes filtering for questions that require tools. A BFCL function-call category therefore does not automatically establish the When2Call tool_call target. Questions answerable from ordinary knowledge require a separate capability-necessity check. The current released generation scripts also have inconsistencies and cannot establish the exact label provenance of the already released SFT data without further verification. These findings rule out fitting a combiner immediately on heuristic SFT plus BFCL labels. The current fixed comparison remains unchanged.

Sources: https://aclanthology.org/anthology-files/pdf/naacl/2025.naacl-long.174.pdf . https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla/main/berkeley-function-call-leaderboard/bfcl_eval/constants/category_mapping.py . https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/When2Call/main/synthetic_data_gen/convert_raw_train_data_to_sft.py .

Analysis: Existing single Jina checkpoint 20261048 and Qwen SFT 1.5B show useful complementary behavior. Their fixed arithmetic probability average improved accuracy from 0.6788061336254108 to 0.6946878422782037 and four-class macro F1 from 0.5050116864318432 to 0.5157041428790551. The gate also improved both metrics. The historical three-encoder expert was stronger alone but its fixed hybrids were weaker than the single-encoder hybrids. No rule or weight was fitted during this comparison. No hidden per-example labels, probabilities, or correctness were exposed. Aggregate baseline accuracies reproduced historical values exactly. Minor historical F1 differences remain, so the common current four-class metric is authoritative for this table.

Next hypothesis: The positive fixed-pair result justifies two distinct parameter-free pooling mechanisms. Geometric pooling tests whether consensus across class probabilities helps. Rank pooling tests robustness to differences in confidence scale. Both will be frozen before a new aggregate measurement. Arithmetic averaging and the confidence gate remain exact controls. A learned router remains deferred until an appropriate unseen calibration source is established.


## Preregistered existing single-encoder fusion comparison

Purpose: Test whether geometric consensus or ordinal Borda rank pooling improves on the strongest existing Jina plus Qwen SFT pair. The prior frozen comparison showed complementary predictions, with equal probability averaging improving accuracy by 58 of 3652 examples. The test set has been inspected in prior work, so this is a fixed aggregate benchmark measurement and not an independent generalization estimate.

Candidates: Existing Jina checkpoint `outputs/clean-validation-cues-lr25e5-smooth0075-seed20261022`, selected historical seed 20261048, and existing Qwen2.5 1.5B SFT adapter `outputs/qwen25-1.5b-sft-when2call`. The single-fusion suite scores each expert once and compares arithmetic probability mean, minimum-entropy gate, equal geometric probability pooling, and equal Borda rank pooling. Geometric pooling clamps probabilities at 1e-8 before taking equal mean log probabilities and softmax. Rank pooling averages tied ranks, sums the two experts’ Borda points, adds 1e-6 times mean probability as a tie break, clamps at 1e-12, and normalizes. The primary method is `single_geometric`.

Selection and data: The fixed pair and four rules are predeclared in code. No training, calibration, weight search, threshold sweep, or candidate selection from test outcomes is allowed. The work directory stores the frozen manifest and artifact hashes before official test loading. The test worker reports aggregate accuracy and four-class macro F1, with present-class macro F1 as a diagnostic only. It must not save or log per-example test labels, probabilities, or correctness.

Exact queued commands:

```text
python -u -m experiments.existing_when2call_hybrid prepare --suite single-fusion --work-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-fusion-20261025 --output-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-fusion-prepare-20261025
python -u -m experiments.existing_when2call_hybrid test --suite single-fusion --work-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-fusion-20261025 --output-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-fusion-test-20261025
```

Environment and controls: The work is supervised by `experiments.watchdog_supervisor` and `experiments.validation_watchdog` at 30-second intervals. The supervisor heartbeat fix is commit `9e5baac2`; the fusion suite is commit `0cddd90b`. Its nine focused unit tests passed before the benchmark run. GPU, runtime, final Git identifier, W&B run, artifact hashes, and aggregate metrics will be added after execution.

## Fixed existing-model fusion comparison, October 25

Purpose: Compare parameter-free combinations of the strongest existing single Jina encoder checkpoint and Qwen SFT 1.5B. The pair was frozen before official test loading. This repeat benchmark is exploratory because historical results have repeatedly inspected this test split.

Setup: Jina checkpoint `outputs/clean-validation-when2call-pref6000-bfcl1500-callonly-seed20261048` and Qwen SFT adapter `outputs/qwen-when2call-sft-15b-seed20261022`, base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, max length 4096, batch size 1, dataset revision `0582f7749df63a96fdc3070932e83e72396ace53`, test/mcq, 3652 rows. Frozen methods were equal arithmetic averaging, minimum-entropy expert selection, equal geometric probability pooling, and equal Borda rank pooling. No weights or thresholds were fitted and no per-example output was saved. RTX A4500. Runtime 459.455 seconds. Code commit `e99541b01db8c88d55c1e4727f90e2db82f702cc`. Frozen config SHA256 `57f19d66117dccd6513511833eb649903709209903e1bc02b0b82966c3793dab`. W&B run `8n2vpvy7`: https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/kunal-personal/when2call-research/runs/8n2vpvy7.

| Method | Accuracy | Macro F1 across four classes | Present-class macro F1 diagnostic |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| single_average | 0.694687842 | 0.515704143 | 0.687605524 |
| single_gate | 0.693044907 | 0.514422081 | 0.685896107 |
| single_geometric | 0.691949617 | 0.513639029 | 0.684852039 |
| single_rank | 0.677984666 | 0.503256048 | 0.671008064 |
| qwen_sft | 0.678806134 | 0.505011686 | 0.673348915 |
| encoder_single | 0.592278204 | 0.439754957 | 0.586339943 |

Analysis: Equal arithmetic averaging remains the best observed result by accuracy and also has the highest macro F1 among these methods. It adds 58 correct predictions over Qwen alone. The geometric and rank pooling hypotheses did not improve the arithmetic control. Selection remains provisional because this benchmark has prior repeated inspections.

Next experiment preregistration: Test a fixed Jina specialist route. Keep Jina's probability vector when its top class is `cannot_answer`; otherwise use Qwen's probability vector. Compare against arithmetic averaging and minimum-entropy gating. The rule transfers the earlier Jina plus Jev class-specialist idea, but its original routing class was chosen from benchmark-label error analysis. No threshold, rule, or parameter will be fitted from this follow-up measurement. Accuracy is the primary optimization objective; macro F1 is reported as a secondary measure. The fixed config is prepared before test loading, which reports aggregate metrics only.

Exact queued commands:

```text
python -u -m experiments.existing_when2call_hybrid prepare --suite single-route --work-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-route-20261025 --output-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-route-prepare-20261025
python -u -m experiments.existing_when2call_hybrid test --suite single-route --work-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-route-20261025 --output-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-route-test-20261025
```

## Fixed class-specialist route comparison, October 25

Purpose: Transfer the earlier encoder plus Jev class-specialist idea to the allowed existing Jina plus Qwen SFT pair. This comparison follows a rule that was inspired by earlier benchmark-label error analysis, so treat it as test-tuned exploratory evidence and not an unbiased generalization estimate.

Setup: Existing Jina checkpoint `outputs/clean-validation-when2call-pref6000-bfcl1500-callonly-seed20261048` and Qwen SFT adapter `outputs/qwen-when2call-sft-15b-seed20261022`, base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, max length 4096, batch size 1, dataset revision `0582f7749df63a96fdc3070932e83e72396ace53`, test/mcq, 3652 examples. Frozen rule: use Jina probabilities if Jina's top class is cannot_answer and Qwen probabilities otherwise. Controls: equal probability average and per-example minimum-entropy expert. No weights or thresholds were fitted. Only aggregate accuracy and macro F1 were saved. RTX A4500. Runtime 480.492 seconds. Code commit `8002c589`. Frozen config SHA256 `022e52c964929761a9b11116bbd08c7c63275fc8bee4970aed9d938a7d7b7f6f`. W&B run `dkkgq6x9`: https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/kunal-personal/when2call-research/runs/dkkgq6x9.

| Method | Accuracy | Macro F1 across four classes | Present-class macro F1 diagnostic |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| single_average | 0.694687842 | 0.515704143 | 0.687605524 |
| single_gate | 0.693044907 | 0.514422081 | 0.685896107 |
| single_encoder_refusal | 0.658269441 | 0.488136876 | 0.650849169 |
| qwen_sft | 0.678806134 | 0.505011686 | 0.673348915 |
| encoder_single | 0.592278204 | 0.439754957 | 0.586339943 |

Analysis: The class-specialist route is worse than Qwen alone by 2.05 percentage points in accuracy and worse than equal averaging by 3.64 points. The encoder's refusal region is not sufficiently reliable to transfer the Jina plus Jev route directly to Jina plus Qwen. Do not use this route as the current candidate.

Next preregistration: Test a fixed asymmetric blend with 25 percent encoder probability and 75 percent Qwen probability. Compare it with equal averaging and minimum-entropy gating. This tests whether shrinking the lower-accuracy standalone encoder toward the stronger Qwen model retains complementary signal with less exposure to encoder errors. The weight is fixed in advance, with no fitting or sweep. Accuracy is the primary objective and macro F1 remains reported.

Exact commands:

```text

python -u -m experiments.existing_when2call_hybrid test --suite single-weighted --work-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-weighted-20261025 --output-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-weighted-test-20261025
```

## Fixed asymmetric encoder Qwen blend, October 25

Purpose: Test whether shrinking the lower-accuracy standalone encoder toward the stronger Qwen SFT model improves the equal-weight ensemble. Candidates were frozen before test loading. The split has prior repeated benchmark inspection, so these are exploratory aggregate measurements.

Setup: Existing Jina checkpoint `outputs/clean-validation-when2call-pref6000-bfcl1500-callonly-seed20261048`, Qwen SFT adapter `outputs/qwen-when2call-sft-15b-seed20261022`, base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, max length 4096, batch size 1, dataset revision `0582f7749df63a96fdc3070932e83e72396ace53`, test/mcq, 3652 examples. Frozen methods were 25 percent encoder plus 75 percent Qwen, equal arithmetic average, and minimum-entropy expert selection. No weights were fitted or swept. Aggregate metrics only. RTX A4500. Runtime 430.920 seconds. Code commit `3c2d624100559734d1756ae5bd138c58e0791621`. Frozen config SHA256 and model hashes are in `outputs/existing-when2call-single-weighted-test-20261025/aggregate-comparison.json`. Preparation W&B `3zuy8ur0`; test W&B `siaty0g5`: https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/kunal-personal/when2call-research/runs/siaty0g5.

| Method | Accuracy | Macro F1 across four classes | Present-class macro F1 diagnostic |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| equal average | 0.694687842 | 0.515704143 | 0.687605524 |
| entropy gate | 0.693044907 | 0.514422081 | 0.685896107 |
| 25 percent encoder, 75 percent Qwen | 0.680996714 | 0.506269371 | 0.675025828 |
| Qwen SFT | 0.678806134 | 0.505011686 | 0.673348915 |
| encoder alone | 0.592278204 | 0.439754957 | 0.586339943 |

Analysis: The asymmetric blend is 0.219 percentage points and 8 correct examples above Qwen alone, but is 1.369 points below equal averaging. Equal averaging remains the accuracy leader by 58 correct examples over Qwen alone. The test does not support shrinking the encoder to 25 percent.

Next comparison: In one frozen scoring pass, test normalized predictive-entropy weighted averaging, top-two-margin weighted averaging, and an encoder override only when its probability margin is at least 0.50 and exceeds Qwen's. Compare with equal averaging and minimum-entropy gating. These are distinct adaptive mechanisms, not a dense sweep. No thresholds are fitted. Accuracy is primary and macro F1 remains reported.

Commands:

```text
python -u -m experiments.existing_when2call_hybrid prepare --suite single-adaptive --work-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-adaptive-20261025 --output-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-adaptive-prepare-20261025
python -u -m experiments.existing_when2call_hybrid test --suite single-adaptive --work-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-adaptive-20261025 --output-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-adaptive-test-20261025
```

## Adaptive existing-model fusion comparison, October 25

Purpose: Compare fixed adaptive methods that let prediction confidence affect the ensemble. The same existing Jina checkpoint and Qwen SFT adapter were used. The official test split has repeated historical inspections, so all results are exploratory aggregate benchmark measurements.

Setup: Jina checkpoint `outputs/clean-validation-when2call-pref6000-bfcl1500-callonly-seed20261048`, Qwen SFT adapter `outputs/qwen-when2call-sft-15b-seed20261022`, base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, max length 4096, batch size 1, revision `0582f7749df63a96fdc3070932e83e72396ace53`, test/mcq, 3652 examples. Methods were equal average, minimum-entropy gate, normalized-entropy weighted average, top-two-margin weighted average, and an encoder override when its margin is at least 0.50 and larger than Qwen’s. No threshold sweep or calibration was used. Aggregate metrics only. RTX A4500, runtime 401.673 seconds. Test W&B run `a8tlnl3p`: https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/kunal-personal/when2call-research/runs/a8tlnl3p. Frozen config SHA256 `782e6dca88f13460f66c3348d3da6e09c9d9966c287d3fd70f5f9a7153aa42a3`.

| Method | Accuracy | Macro F1 across four classes | Present-class macro F1 diagnostic |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| equal average | 0.694687842 | 0.515704143 | 0.687605524 |
| entropy weighted | 0.694414020 | 0.515618388 | 0.687491184 |
| margin weighted | 0.693866375 | 0.515102309 | 0.686803078 |
| entropy gate | 0.693044907 | 0.514422081 | 0.685896107 |
| high-margin encoder override | 0.690306681 | 0.512752246 | 0.683669662 |
| Qwen SFT | 0.678806134 | 0.505011686 | 0.673348915 |
| encoder alone | 0.592278204 | 0.439754957 | 0.586339943 |

Analysis: Entropy weighting nearly matched equal averaging, with one fewer correct example. Margin weighting was three examples lower. The hard encoder override was 16 examples lower than averaging. None replaces the current accuracy leader.

Next experiment preregistration: Rule-based task routing from visible input fields. Test encoder routing for no available tools, at least two tools, short questions of at most 20 words, and long questions over 20 words. Qwen handles rows outside each declared region. Compare with equal averaging and entropy gating. Do not read target fields or use hidden labels to create the masks. Save only aggregate accuracy and macro F1. Accuracy is primary.

Exact queued commands:

```text
python -u -m experiments.existing_when2call_hybrid prepare --suite single-rules --work-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-rules-20261025 --output-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-rules-prepare-20261025
python -u -m experiments.existing_when2call_hybrid test --suite single-rules --work-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-rules-20261025 --output-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-rules-test-20261025
```

## Ensemble exploration backlog

Tested: equal probability averaging; minimum-entropy hard gating; geometric probability pooling; ordinal Borda rank pooling; a Jina cannot_answer specialist route; a 25/75 Jina/Qwen blend; entropy-weighted blending; margin-weighted blending; and a high-margin encoder override. Equal probability averaging remains the accuracy leader at 0.694687842, compared with Qwen SFT at 0.678806134. The class-specialist, geometric, rank, asymmetric, and high-margin variants did not beat the leader.

Queued: rule-based routes by tool availability and question length.

Next distinct families: average raw class logits before softmax; a small predeclared broad weight grid in one model-scoring pass; disagreement-specific routing; input-conditioned mixtures that use tool count and question length jointly; diverse existing encoder-family plus Qwen fusion; and hard-vote or rank-vote variants. Revisit temperature calibration or learned stacking only if we establish a clean calibration split unseen by every fixed member. If the remaining fixed ensemble families plateau, prioritize Qwen SFT data construction and source-mixture experiments, then return to ensemble scoring with the improved model. This is an ordered exploration queue, not a stop rule.

## Input-feature rule routing comparison, October 25

Purpose: Test whether visible question and tool structure can select the Jina encoder for a subset of inputs while Qwen handles the rest. The four rules were frozen before official test loading. The benchmark has prior repeated inspections, so this is exploratory aggregate evidence.

Setup: Jina checkpoint `outputs/clean-validation-when2call-pref6000-bfcl1500-callonly-seed20261048`, Qwen SFT adapter `outputs/qwen-when2call-sft-15b-seed20261022`, base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, max length 4096, batch size 1, dataset revision `0582f7749df63a96fdc3070932e83e72396ace53`, test/mcq, 3652 rows. Rules route to Jina when there are no available tools, when there are at least two tools, when the question has at most 20 words, or when it has more than 20 words; Qwen handles other rows. Controls are equal probability averaging and minimum-entropy gating. Rules use visible inputs only, never labels. Aggregate metrics only. RTX A4500, runtime 429.926 seconds. Test W&B run `7h1eswyz`: https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/kunal-personal/when2call-research/runs/7h1eswyz. The asynchronous recorder reported a temporary Git index lock; the result and its failure note are preserved in local commit `3b647a14`.

| Method | Accuracy | Macro F1 across four classes | Present-class macro F1 diagnostic |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| equal average | 0.694687842 | 0.515704143 | 0.687605524 |
| entropy gate | 0.693044907 | 0.514422081 | 0.685896107 |
| encoder on no-tools rows | 0.679079956 | 0.505149525 | 0.673532700 |
| Qwen SFT | 0.678806134 | 0.505011686 | 0.673348915 |
| encoder on long questions | 0.652245345 | 0.484299297 | 0.645732397 |
| encoder on short questions | 0.618838992 | 0.460578096 | 0.614104128 |
| encoder on many-tools rows | 0.604874042 | 0.449079079 | 0.598772106 |
| encoder alone | 0.592278204 | 0.439754957 | 0.586339943 |

Analysis: No simple input-type rule improved on averaging. The no-tools route was only one example above Qwen alone. All other rules reduced accuracy. These partitions do not support a broad input-based expert switch. More specific structured disagreement and tool-count combinations remain untested.

Next fixed comparison: Score encoder probability weights 0.10, 0.25, 0.40, 0.60, 0.75, and 0.90, alongside equal averaging and entropy gating. Also compare 25/75 and 75/25 weighted geometric pooling and standardized log-probability averaging. All weights and rules are frozen before data loading. This batch tests probability weighting, product pooling, and score-scale normalization in one pair of model passes. Accuracy is primary and macro F1 remains reported.

Commands:

```text
python -u -m experiments.existing_when2call_hybrid prepare --suite single-pool-grid --work-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-pool-grid-20261025 --output-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-pool-grid-prepare-20261025
python -u -m experiments.existing_when2call_hybrid test --suite single-pool-grid --work-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-pool-grid-20261025 --output-dir outputs/existing-when2call-single-pool-grid-test-20261025
```

## qwen-pref-control-continue-apigenmt500-seed20261047 stop-rule correction

The first completed evaluation at step 397 had clean preference validation accuracy/macro F1 0.846111/0.635981 and aggregate black-box test accuracy/macro F1 0.587897/0.431152. The starting aggregate test accuracy was 0.666210. The drop was 0.078313, greater than the newly specified 0.02 threshold. The process had started its step-794 isolated test evaluation when the user changed the rule. That measurement was interrupted, and the run was stopped. Test labels were never exposed. The first checkpoint's training probe and APIGen source validation were entirely request-for-information examples, so the result is parser/sample-skewed.

BFCL Live to When2Call action-label augmentation, GPT-6 Luna, 2026-10-26
Purpose: Label source-disjoint BFCL Live examples with the reviewed four-way When2Call action prompt and form an augmented-data train/validation split.
Sources: Current official Gorilla BFCL_v4_live_{simple,multiple,parallel,parallel_multiple,relevance,irrelevance}.json files. Source-ID matching used the public When2Call test/mcq source_id values and question text only. Test labels and answer choices were not loaded or sent to the labeling API.
Overlap procedure: The When2Call MCQ test file has 3,652 rows and 1,295 unique BFCL source IDs. Of 2,251 BFCL rows, 956 had no source-ID match. Excluded 34 additional question near-duplicates using normalized character four-gram Jaccard similarity >= 0.80 against the test questions, leaving 922 examples. Candidate categories: Multiple 16, Parallel 15, Parallel Multiple 24, Relevance 16, Irrelevance 851.
Labeling: GPT-6 Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) via OpenAI Responses API, reasoning effort none, JSON-schema constrained labels, 24 concurrent requests, up to 5 retries. Prompt: prompts/bfcl_to_when2call_labels.md, SHA-256 2a191a61da8709a4cff51676bfb421c274e5e84b7c81ee3a7e6d44f80cf8fa85. Source code: experiments/label_bfcl_when2call_api.py, commit 126b3338. All 922 examples received one of A/B/C/D; 85 also carry needs_review=true and are retained in the requested full corpus with that flag visible.
Label distribution: direct 311, tool_call 128, request_for_info 212, cannot_answer 271. Stratified held-out split seed 20261025: training 738 (direct 249, tool_call 102, request_for_info 170, cannot_answer 217); validation 184 (direct 62, tool_call 26, request_for_info 42, cannot_answer 54). Category-label counts: Multiple tool_call 16; Parallel tool_call 15; Parallel Multiple tool_call 24; Relevance tool_call 10 and request_for_info 6; Irrelevance direct 311, tool_call 63, request_for_info 206, cannot_answer 271.
Artifacts: data/bfcl_when2call_labeled.jsonl and data/bfcl_when2call_labeled.metadata.json. Labeled JSONL SHA-256 a4b817a01c109603c00fe9e682f11eb636afc139894a92d4960bde8bddfda27f. No When2Call test labels were read for these labels or for the split. Limitations: Labels are GPT-6 Luna judgments. Some Irrelevance rows received tool_call or request_for_info because the prompt asks the model to inspect each example rather than force a category-to-label mapping; 85 rows are flagged for review. This is the labeling distribution, not evidence that training on these labels improves test performance.

Prompt-alignment audit caveat: The partial GPT-6 Luna alignment audit measured 71.04% on 3,470 completed When2Call test variants, with 182 unprocessed after cancellation. The BFCL category therefore may not describe the visible tool set in these transformed examples. Treat the reported partial alignment as a diagnostic under those inputs, not a valid estimate of labeling accuracy on intact BFCL Live examples. Do not tune labels or prompts from that test score.

Base Qwen 1.5B SFT on a balanced BFCL and When2Call mix, 2026-10-26
Purpose: Measure whether the labeled BFCL Live examples can train a fresh Qwen model in a balanced mixture with original When2Call data.
Setup: Base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` with a fresh LoRA adapter. Loss was logged per optimizer step. Full evaluation ran at baseline, step 1,000, and epoch end at step 1,476.
Data: BFCL labeled file `data/bfcl_when2call_labeled.jsonl`, SHA-256 `a4b817a01c109603c00fe9e682f11eb636afc139894a92d4960bde8bddfda27f`, original prompt SHA-256 `2a191a61da8709a4cff51676bfb421c274e5e84b7c81ee3a7e6d44f80cf8fa85`. The fixed BFCL split contributed 738 train and 184 validation rows. The original When2Call split used seed 20261029, with 7,200 train and 1,800 validation rows. A deterministic stratified 738-row train sample and 184-row validation sample were selected using seeds 20261050 and 20261051. Validation was 50/50 by source, 184 BFCL plus 184 original examples. Original train sample fingerprint `4e22c5b6f77e84d92f1eaf595281597726718e160e39e6f8a0a6185c8be0399d`; original validation sample fingerprint `ff5b05e683ec7e0047f1c391d8b75687b43e78a7e0f513b1c750e11f3ea7ec9f`.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| Step 1,000 | 0.6531 / 0.5702 | 0.5734 / 0.4756 | 0.4511 / 0.3880 | 0.6957 / 0.5180 | 0.5148 / 0.3840 |
| Step 1,476 | 0.7771 / 0.7696 | 0.6495 / 0.6375 | 0.5489 / 0.5246 | 0.7500 / 0.5639 | 0.5296 / 0.4048 |

The step-1,476 checkpoint had the best balanced validation accuracy and was selected by that validation metric. Relative to step 1,000, aggregate test accuracy rose by 1.48 percentage points and macro F1 rose by 2.07 points. Training accuracy was 77.71%, balanced validation accuracy was 64.95%, BFCL validation accuracy was 54.89%, and original validation accuracy was 75.00%. The gap between the two validation sources shows that generated BFCL label validation is the harder source and may reflect label noise or a distribution difference.
Test handling: The official 3,652-row When2Call test set was scored only for aggregate accuracy and macro F1 at baseline and checkpoints. Test labels were not used for checkpoint selection, and no individual test examples or predictions were saved.
Artifacts and environment: Metrics are in `outputs/qwen-bfcl-original-5050-base-seed20261050/metrics.json`; checkpoints are in that directory. Limitations: There was no same-budget original-only control in this run. The historical best used 7,200 original training rows plus Glaive examples, so this experiment does not establish that adding generated BFCL labels improves over a size-matched original-only training set. A matched control is needed to isolate BFCL data value.

Evaluation-sample cap update, 2026-10-26
The user clarified that the second and third queued experiments should skip held-out validation and report only training and aggregate black-box test metrics. Training metrics will use a deterministic random sample of 500 rows per epoch; the complete test set will still be evaluated. The trainer supports `--validation-source none`, samples at most 500 training examples, and caps any requested validation sample at 500. The first 738-row BFCL run was already in its final evaluation when this guidance arrived. Its loaded code evaluates all 738 training rows and cannot be changed without interrupting the authorized run, so it is being allowed to finish under its original configuration. The new 500-row cap applies to the two pending runs and subsequent runs.

Full-data BFCL comparison outcomes and evidence audit, 2026-10-26
The first three requested fresh-base runs have completed. Accuracy and macro F1 are shown below.

| Experiment | Epoch | Training evaluation | Clean held-out validation | Aggregate black-box test |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BFCL only, 738 rows | 1 | 0.7344 / 0.7043 on 738 rows | 0.5924 / 0.5617 on 368 rows, including 184 BFCL and 184 When2Call examples | 0.4551 / 0.3307 on all 3,652 test rows |
| Full When2Call `train_pref`, 9,000 rows | 1 | 0.9220 / 0.6917 on 500 rows | Skipped as directed | 0.6706 / 0.5002 on all 3,652 test rows |
| Full When2Call `train_pref`, 9,000 rows | 2 | 0.9600 / 0.7201 on 500 rows | Skipped as directed | 0.7024 / 0.5278 on all 3,652 test rows |
| Full When2Call plus all BFCL, 9,922 rows | 1 | 0.9000 / 0.8966 on 500 rows | Missing and queued for post hoc measurement | 0.6520 / 0.4947 on all 3,652 test rows |
| Full When2Call plus all BFCL, 9,922 rows | 2 | 0.9440 / 0.9426 on 500 rows | Missing and queued for post hoc measurement | 0.6402 / 0.4739 on all 3,652 test rows |

The most recent experiment has training and aggregate black-box test evidence for both epochs but no clean held-out validation. The fixed 500-row stratified sample from the separate `nvidia/When2Call:train_sft` config will be evaluated on both saved checkpoints before a new training experiment. That sample includes the sole direct-answer row but has no tool-call rows. The validation result is post hoc and will not be used to select a checkpoint based on any test labels. Test outputs remain aggregate-only.

A new hypothesis is that a small BFCL fraction can retain some source diversity while reducing overfit to generated labels. Supporting development evidence includes the 738-row BFCL-only run's 0.7344 training accuracy versus 0.5924 balanced validation accuracy. The next experiment after the missing validation measurement is a fresh-base 1,476-row mixture with 10% BFCL and 90% When2Call examples. It will evaluate a fixed 500-row training probe, 368-row balanced held-out validation, and the complete test set every epoch, with early stopping on validation accuracy only.

Post hoc clean validation completed for the full When2Call plus full BFCL experiment, 2026-10-26
Purpose: Fill the missing clean held-out validation evidence before starting another training experiment.
Source: A deterministic stratified 500-row sample from the separate `nvidia/When2Call:train_sft` configuration, seed 20261057, fingerprint `1ce21c31939384815b93e6eacbbf484924e32f2f28972ddbe2004303a2945bd6`. The sample has 250 cannot-answer, 249 request-for-information, one direct-answer, and zero tool-call rows. The source is independent of the 9,000 `train_pref` rows and BFCL training data.

| Checkpoint | Training accuracy / macro F1 on 500 rows | Clean validation accuracy / macro F1 on 500 rows | Aggregate test accuracy / macro F1 on 3,652 rows |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Epoch 1 | 0.9000 / 0.8966 | 0.9280 / 0.4774 | 0.6520 / 0.4947 |
| Epoch 2 | 0.9440 / 0.9426 | 0.9100 / 0.4729 | 0.6402 / 0.4739 |

Validation was measured after the fixed two-epoch schedule and was not used to select training duration. Macro F1 includes all four declared classes; the validation sample has no tool-call rows, so this score is limited for that class. Test metrics remain aggregate-only and were not used for selection. The primary metrics artifact now contains all three evidence types for both epochs.


Duplicate worker attempt for the low-dose BFCL experiment, 2026-10-26
A stale PID in `logs/research_state.json` caused the watchdog to launch a second copy of the 10% BFCL experiment against the same output directory. Duplicate W&B run `m4pemqs1` failed after seven optimizer updates with a `heartbeat.tmp` `FileNotFoundError`. It saved no checkpoint and performed no training probe, clean validation, or test measurement. The original worker (PID 103361, W&B run `9kho1als`) continued. The state now tracks the original worker, and the next run remains queued behind it.

Primary metrics artifact integrity correction, 2026-10-26
The separate post hoc validation artifact remains intact with the 500-row validation measurements for epochs 1 and 2. The primary training metrics file was found without those attached values during the latest audit. Reattached the same recorded validation results from the post hoc artifact. This did not run a new evaluation or change any result or selection.

Full When2Call training with clean validation-based stopping, 2026-10-26
Purpose: Determine how long full `train_pref` SFT should continue using clean held-out validation accuracy, while reporting full aggregate test metrics only.
Setup: Fresh Qwen 2.5 1.5B base, all 9,000 When2Call `train_pref` rows, LoRA rank 16, batch size 1, learning rate 2e-5, weight decay 0.01, max 10 epochs, stopping at the first epoch without validation-accuracy improvement. Training and validation probes each use 500 deterministic examples. Validation is a separate 500-row sample from `nvidia/When2Call:train_sft`, seed 20261064. The complete 3,652-row test set is evaluated after each epoch.

| Epoch | Training accuracy / macro F1 | Clean validation accuracy / macro F1 | Aggregate test accuracy / macro F1 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 0.9280 / 0.6960 | 0.9080 / 0.4713 | 0.6673 / 0.4849 |
| 2 | 0.9520 / 0.7142 | 0.9400 / 0.4805 | 0.6958 / 0.5211 |
| 3 | 0.9760 / 0.7320 | 0.9420 / 0.4834 | 0.6922 / 0.5111 |
| 4 | 0.9860 / 0.7395 | 0.9280 / 0.4774 | 0.6544 / 0.4680 |

Training stopped after the epoch-4 validation-accuracy decline. The best clean validation checkpoint is epoch 3 at 0.9420 accuracy and 0.4834 macro F1. The training probe kept improving while validation accuracy fell by 1.4 percentage points at epoch 4. The validation sample has no tool-call rows and one direct-answer row. Test results are aggregate-only and were not used for stopping or selection.

Ensemble candidate selected on capped clean validation, 2026-10-26
On 500 deterministic stratified `train_sft` validation examples, Qwen epoch 2 scored 0.9560 accuracy / 0.9715 macro F1; the encoder scored 0.8940 / 0.9326; equal probability averaging scored 0.9480 / 0.9671. The highest fixed-candidate validation accuracy was 0.9640 / 0.9757 for `single_request_conf_80`, a four-example or 0.8-point improvement over Qwen. The rule uses encoder probabilities only for predictions of request_for_info with maximum probability at least 0.80, and Qwen otherwise. This rule was selected by clean validation only. Twenty-eight fixed candidates were screened on the same 500 examples, so its gain may reflect validation overfitting. A single full-test aggregate measurement is queued for report only.

Cross-split clean-validation confirmation, 2026-10-26
On the second deterministic 500-row clean `train_sft` sample, Qwen scored 0.9360 accuracy / 0.9570 macro F1, the encoder scored 0.9220 / 0.9489, equal average scored 0.9480 / 0.9663, and request_for_info confidence routing at threshold 0.60 scored 0.9500 / 0.9636. The 0.60 route improved over Qwen on both clean samples. It is frozen for one aggregate test measurement. The threshold-0.80 route test tied Qwen at 0.70235 accuracy; its macro F1 was 0.52824 versus 0.52779. Test metrics remain report-only.

The lower-scoring one-shot and three-shot variants were not evaluated on test.

## OpenAI retrieval source and K screen, queued 2026-10-27

Purpose: Test whether OpenAI embedding retrieval improves the strongest standalone Qwen model, and whether the retrieval source, embedded fields, or number of demonstrations matters.

Prior evidence audit: The latest completed retrieval run has linked Qwen epoch-2 training-probe metrics (500 examples, accuracy 0.960000, macro F1 0.720145, loss 0.408354), clean-validation metrics (500 examples, see `outputs/when2call-dynamic-retrieval-clean-20270327/metrics.json`), and the existing aggregate black-box Qwen report (3652 examples, accuracy 0.702629, macro F1 0.527976). No evidence measurement was missing for the clean-selected zero-shot candidate. The old retrieved-prompt comparison is not considered valid because its demo label mapping was reversed.

Queued setup: Qwen2.5-1.5B epoch-2 adapter. OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`, 1536 dimensions. Retrieval pools are `train_sft`, `train_pref`, and a preference-first union deduplicated by normalized question. Input representations are question-only, tool-schema-only, and question plus tools. Test Qwen K=1, 2, and 3 demonstrations and separate direct label votes at K=1, 3, and 5. Cap clean validation at 500. Exclude questions from the full clean-development split from all retrieval pools. Cache embedding artifacts by model, feature representation, role, and ordered input digest. Evaluate one clean sample with split/sample seeds 20270327/20270332, then replicate with sample seed 20270334. Choose candidates by clean validation only. Test metrics remain report-only.

## Completed OpenAI retrieval screen and required aggregate measurement

The screen completed on 500 clean validation examples. The clean-selected baseline was corrected-mapping zero-shot Qwen at 0.942 accuracy and 0.967059 macro F1. The best retrieved prompt was train_sft tools-only K=3 at 0.816 accuracy and 0.839697 macro F1. Source checkpoint training evidence is linked to `outputs/qwen-when2call-fullpool-base-seed20261055/metrics.json` (epoch 2, 500-example probe, accuracy 0.960000, macro F1 0.720145, loss 0.408354). A matching aggregate black-box measurement is missing because the existing Qwen report uses a different prompt order. The corrected zero-shot test measurement is queued before further queued experiments, after the clean replication that had already started. The test evaluator saves only aggregate metrics and source training evidence. Test labels remain report-only.

## Similarity-gated retrieval fallback, queued

Hypothesis: Retrieval may harm low-similarity queries but help where the nearest train_sft tool-schema example is strongly related. After the required corrected-mapping aggregate test measurement and existing queue, compare zero-shot, always-retrieve K=3, and zero-shot fallback gates at the 50th, 75th, and 90th percentile of unlabeled clean-validation similarity scores. Use text-embedding-3-small, tool-schema-only retrieval, and 500 clean validation examples. Select only on clean validation.

## Seed-only repeats discontinued

The user directed that experiments must not be repeated with different seeds as a default. The active 27-combination clean-validation replication was stopped before completion. Two queued seed-only repetitions, one using another 500-row sample and one using a new split, were removed. No metrics from the stopped replication are treated as completed results. Future work will change a substantive method component instead. The corrected zero-shot aggregate baseline measurement and distinct embedding, prompt-length, and similarity-gating hypotheses remain queued.

WHEN2CALL RETRIEVAL EVIDENCE AUDIT
Experiment: when2call-similarity-gate-pref-only-k3-fallback-test-20270425
Purpose: Compare preference-only nearest-example retrieval with the frozen Qwen epoch-2 classifier.
Setup: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct adapter outputs/qwen-when2call-fullpool-base-seed20261055/epoch-02; train_pref retrieval pool (8,068 examples); text-embedding-3-small, 1,536 dimensions, tools_only feature; K=3 with K=1 fallback on label disagreement; probability average with retrieval weight 0.5; clean-selected absolute-similarity gate at quantile 0.7.
Selection: The gate and threshold were selected on 500 clean train_sft validation examples. A fixed 500-row test sample was chosen by row index with seed 20270425. No individual test labels or outcomes were used for candidate selection. Aggregate test metrics only were saved.
Training evidence: Frozen checkpoint epoch-2 probe on 500 examples, accuracy 0.9600, macro F1 0.72015, loss 0.40835. Source: outputs/qwen-when2call-fullpool-base-seed20261055/metrics.json. No training occurred in this retrieval experiment.
Clean validation: 500 examples. Selected gate accuracy 0.9480, macro F1 0.97116. Zero-shot accuracy 0.9420, macro F1 0.96706. Source: outputs/when2call-similarity-gate-pref-only-k3-fallback-20270424/metrics.json.
Black-box test: Sample of 500, selected gate accuracy 0.6740, macro F1 0.50691; zero-shot 0.6700, 0.50430. Full aggregate on 3,652 examples, selected gate accuracy 0.68593, macro F1 0.51572; zero-shot 0.68045, 0.51193. Source: outputs/when2call-similarity-gate-pref-only-k3-fallback-test-20270425/metrics.json.
Artifacts: W&B run ybszmhvt. The test file stores aggregate metrics without per-example outcomes.

Experiment: when2call-similarity-gate-30pct-pref-k3-qwen-match-fulltest-20270520

## qwen-when2call-aug-tool-order-20261027 epoch-01 checkpoint

Purpose: Test whether label-preserving tool-order permutations improve Qwen generalization from the 9,000 When2Call `train_pref` examples. Setup: start from `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` with fresh rank-16 LoRA, learning rate 2e-5, weight decay 0.01, batch size 1, seed 20261055. Append one deterministically shuffled tool-order variant for every preference row with more than one tool. The source has 9,000 rows, of which 5,803 received variants, for 14,803 training rows. Evaluate up to 500 training rows, 500 held-out `train_sft` rows, and all 3,652 black-box test rows. Use clean validation for continuation and candidate selection. The full test measurement is report-only.

Epoch 1 checkpoint: loss 0.566216, training accuracy 0.956000, training macro F1 0.717235; clean validation accuracy 0.946000, macro F1 0.483559; aggregate black-box test accuracy 0.668127, macro F1 0.468839. W&B run `cxm2b3nx`: https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/kunal-personal/when2call-research/runs/cxm2b3nx. The run remains active for epoch 2. No individual test outcomes were accessed or saved.

## qwen-when2call-aug-tool-order-20261027 final results

Purpose and setup are recorded in the epoch-01 entry above. The experiment trained the 9,000 When2Call preference rows plus 5,803 deterministic tool-order variants for two epochs from the same fresh Qwen 1.5B LoRA setup. Training and clean validation used 500 examples per epoch. The black-box test used all 3,652 examples. W&B run: cxm2b3nx (https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/kunal-personal/when2call-research/runs/cxm2b3nx).

| Epoch | Train accuracy | Train macro F1 | Clean validation accuracy | Clean validation macro F1 | Aggregate test accuracy | Aggregate test macro F1 | Training loss |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.9560 | 0.717235 | 0.9460 | 0.483559 | 0.668127 | 0.468839 | 0.566216 |
| 2 | 0.9820 | 0.736828 | 0.9480 | 0.485551 | 0.659365 | 0.468468 | 0.266147 |

Clean validation improved from 0.946 to 0.948, so the run completed its planned second epoch. Test metrics are report-only. Test accuracy decreased by 0.877 percentage points from epoch 1 to epoch 2 and remains below the known standalone Qwen benchmark. No test labels selected the checkpoint.

## synthetic-data-generation-pilot-20261028

Purpose: Create small in-distribution synthetic training pilots to test distinct example-construction strategies.

Setup: GPT-6 Luna Responses API. Source: only `nvidia/When2Call:train_pref` (9,000 rows). Four strategies requested 50 examples each: new tool calls over an existing schema set, missing required information, unsupported capabilities, and tool calls over composed tool sets. Each generation request ran under an asynchronous semaphore with concurrency 24. Each candidate passed structural checks and a separate GPT-6 Luna action-label judgment. Run cost cap: $1.00. Lifetime authorized generation cap: $10.00. No test data or labels were loaded.

Accepted examples: 49 new tool-call, 31 request-for-information, 50 cannot-answer, and 50 composed-tool-call examples, for 180 total. The request-for-information pilot accepted fewer examples because schema validation rejected missing fields with defaults and malformed argument sets. The API ledger records 455 requests, 338,901 input tokens, 34,447 output tokens, two errors, and estimated cost $0.0511136.

Status: Generation completed in approximately two minutes. Four separate one-epoch Qwen pilots are queued. The first run uses original preference data plus the 49 new-tool-call examples. Training and clean-validation probes are capped at 500 examples. The initial aggregate-only black-box screen is capped at 500 rows; full evaluation is reserved for promising candidates.
